articles.title: Upcoming New DC Movies and TV Shows: 2026 Release Dates and Beyond
articles.summary: Here's a look at all the DC movies and series currently in the works, along with a few whose fates may be in jeopardy.
articles.body:
A lot is changing for DC's lineup of movies and shows in the years ahead. James Gunn and Peter Safran, co-CEOs of DC Studios, have a strategy for a more cohesive and interconnected lineup of content moving forward. It all starts with Chapter 1, dubbed "Gods and Monsters."

It can be very difficult to keep track of all the big changes at DC these days. And Gunn is always dropping updates and news it seems, including the reveal of his Superman follow-up Man of Tomorrow ! That's why we've put together this comprehensive list of everything currently in the works, as well as the major projects that have either been officially canceled or gone dormant.

Come join us in the reborn DC Universe. Click on through the slideshow below for a glimpse or read on for even more details...

What Are the Next DC Movies Coming Out? 2026 Release Dates

DC Universe: Every Upcoming Movie and TV Show

For those keeping track, here's the full lineup of upcoming DC movies and TV shows:

Dynamic Duo (Animated Robin Origin Movie) (June 30, 2028)

Mister Miracle Animated Series (In Production)

The People v. Gorilla Grodd TV Series (In Development)

Batman: The Brave and the Bold (In Development)

Creature Commandos Season 2 (In Development)

Blue Beetle Animated Series (In Development)

Harley Quinn and Other Animated Titles (In Development)

V for Vendetta TV Series (In Development)

The Authority (No Longer in Development)

Waller TV Series (No Longer in Development)

Booster Gold TV Series (No Longer in Development)

Paradise Lost TV Series (No Longer in Development)

Here are some of the most notable projects that are currently in the works:

A Clayface movie scripted by Mike Flanagan is moving fast at DC. Flanagan (The Haunting of Hill House, Doctor Sleep, etc.) previously voiced a desire to make a Clayface movie as a "horror/thriller/tragedy." However, due to his various TV commitments, he won't direct the film, with Speak No Evil's James Watkins expected to direct for a Fall, 2026, release. Tom Rhys Harries stars as the titular villain. Safran and Gunn promise a body horror picture that is R-rated as well.

Given Deadline's previous report that Clayface is one of the major villains debuting in The Batman Part II , and the fact that the Clayface movie is being produced by Matt Reeves and Lynn Harris' 6th & Idaho Productions, it had been assumed that this movie would be set in The Batman universe rather than the DCU. But Gunn has since said that it is in fact unrelated to The Batman Epic Crime Saga and is definitely part of the DCU. Presumably, those earlier reports of the character being in The Batman Part II will wind up not panning out at this point.

We've known for a while that James Gunn is working on his first post-Superman movie in the DCU, but it seems like he won't be venturing too far from the beaten path. Warner Bros. CEO David Zaslav revealed on an investor call , "We're thrilled to share that James Gunn is already writing and preparing to direct the next installment within the 'Super-Family.'" Previously, Gunn told EW that his next project isn't exactly Superman 2, saying, "Is it a straight-up Superman sequel? I would not say necessarily."

Gunn surprised DC fans by tweeting out the title and release date of the film. Man of Tomorrow will hit theaters on July 9, 2027, almost exactly two years after Superman's release. The accompanying Jim Lee artwork suggests the film will focus on an alliance between David Corenswet's Man of Steel and Nicholas Hoult's Lex Luthor, as the two confront a common enemy (Brainiac? General Zod? Doomsday?). We wouldn't be at all surprised if the film also stars Milly Alcock's Supergirl, along with potentially other members of the Superman extended family (Steel? Superboy? Mon-El?).

According to James Gunn, Dynamic Duo will tell the origin story of not one but two Robins -- Dick Grayson and Jason Todd. The film will be directed by Arthur Mintz, who's making the picture with his new animation studio Swaybox using a mix of animation, puppetry, CGI, and live-action performance. Huh.

Of course The Batman Part II is in the works with Matt Reeves returning to write and direct and Robert Pattinson putting on the cape, cowl, and eyeliner (!) again as the Dark Knight Detective. The film is confirmed to have survived the recent turmoil at Warner Bros. Discovery , and Reeves has even signed a multi-year first-look deal with the studio. There's no word yet on what it will be about, so begin your Joker speculation now. The release date of the film has been pushed a couple of times now, first from October 2025 to October 2026, and then to October 2027... and then to February 18, 2028.

James Gunn has also confirmed that Pattinson will not be the DCU's version of Batman .

Mister Miracle is the second animated series to be produced under the DC Studios banner, following 2024's Creature Commandos. The series will be helmed by showrunner and producer Tom King, who previously penned 2017's Mister Miracle comic. The animated series looks to be directly based on that comic, which deals with Scott Free's attempts to make sense of his reality during a destructive war between Apokolips and New Genesis.

HBO Max has given the go-ahead on the eight-episode, half-hour comedy series The People v. Gorilla Grodd, which will be done in the style of true-crime series. Superman's Jimmy Olsen (Skyler Gisondo) "hosts" the show, which will focus on the DC supervillain Gorilla Grodd (yes, the super-smart, talking gorilla). American Vandal mockumentary experts Tony Yacenda and Dan Perrault will write, produce, and serve as showrunners, with Jimmy Tatro playing Grodd and Superman actors Beck Bennett, Mikaela Hoover, and Wendell Pierce reprising their roles as Steve Lombard, Cat Grant, and Perry White respectively.

We finally got that oft-promised Green Lantern show. Lanterns is a high-concept detective drama in the vein of True Detective that revolves around Hal Jordan and John Stewart. Kyle Chandler (Friday Night Lights) plays Hal and Aaron Pierre (The Underground Railroad) is John. Kelly Macdonald also stars. A second season is said to be in the works.

DC has confirmed that we'll have two cinematic versions of Batman going forward, as the DCU will get its own Dark Knight alongside the standalone movies of Matt Reeves' The Batman series. The Brave and the Bold looks to deal with the full Bat-family, centering specifically on Bruce Wayne's 10-year-old son Damian. The movie will draw heavily from Grant Morrison's Batman comics. It is unclear how the film will connect to the events of The Flash movie, if at all (probably not?), but that film's director, Andy Muschietti, was at one point confirmed to be directing The Brave and the Bold .

More recently, it seems that Gunn and Safran have put some distance between the project and Muschietti, with Gunn taking point on it. “Everybody knows I love Batman and it’s important to me so I’m working very closely with the writer on Brave and the Bold,” he told a group of reporters in February, 2025. Once the script is completed (it is not currently known who the writer is), Gunn and Safran said they will take it to Muschietti "and see if it's a fit for him."

James Gunn's latest band of misfit superheroes, the Creature Commandos, kicked off the new DCU with the first season of their animated series on Max, and a Season 2 is already in the planning stages. What the new version of the team will look like remains to be seen, though the Creature Commandos Season 1 finale did give us some hints...

Swamp Thing may not have found much success on the short-lived DC Universe app, but DC was betting big on this lumbering monster for their new cinematic universe when they announced their plans for the new movie slate in 2023. The Swamp Thing movie was to explore the dark origins of Alec Holland's monstrous alter ego, with Logan and Indiana Jones 5 director James Mangold writing the script for the film.

However, more recently Gunn and Safran have said that Swamp Thing hasn't had much movement as Mangold was working on his Bob Dylan movie, A Complete Unknown. "We hope that he'll come back to Swamp Thing when he's ready, because again, that was one of those ones that we love him as a filmmaker, so we're happy to wait for him," said Safran. Gunn added that the main reason they pursued the project was because "James came to us with it, frankly."

The Teen Titans are returning to live-action following the conclusion of Max's Titans series. As reported by THR, a new Teen Titans movie is in the works , with the screenplay being penned by Supergirl: Woman of Tomorrow writer Ana Nogueira. It's unknown whether the movie is meant to be part of the DCU or a standalone project.

The Hollywood Reporter broke the news that DC Studios is developing a villain-centric team-up movie featuring Bane and Deathstroke . The film is being written by Matthew Orton (Captain America: Brave New World). It's unclear whether the project is set in James Gunn's DCU, the world of Matt Reeves' The Batman, or an entirely standalone universe a la Joker.

Gunn recently confirmed to EW that a new Wonder Woman movie is in the works as part of the DCU, saying, "Wonder Woman's being written right now." The movie is a separate project from the previously announced Paradise Lost series. Presumably, Wonder Woman will reboot the franchise with a new lead actress rather than bring back Gal Gadot's Diana.

A Blue Beetle animated TV show is reportedly in development. Xolo Maridueña, who played the title hero in the live-action movie, says he'll be back to voice Jaime Reyes for the series.

Warner Bros. has a variety of animated properties in various stages of development as streaming series (in addition to their never-ending DTV animated movie releases). That includes a fifth season of Harley Quinn which debuted in January, 2025, on Max, a possible ninth season of Teen Titans Go!, a third season of Adult Swim/Max's My Adventures With Superman, Season 2 of Amazon Prime's Batman: Caped Crusader (from Bruce Timm, J. J. Abrams, and Matt Reeves), and upcoming series such as Blue Beetle, My Adventures With Green Lantern (featuring the Jessica Cruz Lantern), DC Super Powers, Starfire, and Mister Miracle.

After decades in development hell through various studio regimes and stars attached to it, it seemed like Sgt. Rock was finally coming to the big screen. DC Studios co-CEOs James Gunn and Peter Safran acknowledged the project was in development with Luca Guadagnino directing. Guadagnino (Queer, Call Me By Your Name, Suspiria, Challengers) isn't exactly the first name you'd expect to hear for a Sgt. Rock movie so it made it an even more exciting prospect.

After rumors of Daniel Craig playing the title role in the WWII movie were shot down by Gunn, it was reported that Colin Farrell was cast instead. The project was to shoot in Summer 2025 for a Fall 2026 release but as soon as Sgt. Rock finally came together, the project fell apart. Still, Gunn has said that the film is still in development, though it remains to be seen who would star or direct if it happens.

In November of 2025, Variety reported that Pete Jackson ( not the Lord of the Rings luminary) is attached to write a TV series adaptation for HBO of Alan Moore and David Lloyd's acclaimed comic about a dystopic near-future where the anarchist known only as V battles the oppresive government. James Gunn and Peter Safran will executive produce the series, among others, if it moves forward beyond the writing stage.

Keanu Reeves was reportedly going to reprise his iconic DC role at one point. A sequel to 2005's Constantine was in the news in 2022, with Reeves set to star and Francis Lawrence returning as director. The screenplay was being written by Akiva Goldsman, and Goldsman was also producing the film alongside Bad Robot’s J.J. Abrams and Hannah Minghella. Lawrence gave IGN an update on the project when we spoke to him in May 2025 for The Long Walk :

"Constantine 2 is a real thing. It is something that we have been working on and trying to crack and figure things out over the years. And with all the various regime changes and things at Warner Brothers and who has rights to DC characters/Vertigo characters and DC Dark and all that, the character of Constantine has kind of changed hands over the years, which became roadblocks for us. We now are past those roadblocks, and so Keanu and Akiva ... who I did Constantine and I Am Legend with, have an idea, and Akiva is actually writing a script. And I'm really excited about the idea, and Keanu is really excited about the idea, but we've all collaborated on it and he is off writing, and so fingers crossed we can really get that going. I think we're all super excited and this is definitely the closest we've been in the 20 years since the movie came out."

DC's anti-Justice League were a big part of the initial announcement line-up that Gunn and Safran made back in 2023, but it seems like the project has been a tougher script to crack than they expected. The Authority is a group of powerful heroes who take a far more proactive approach to meting out justice, but Gunn said in February, 2025, that it's been “the one that's been the hardest, both because of the shifting overall story and because of getting it right in a world with The Boys and a world with all the things that The Authority influenced that came out after it.” The project is now on the “back burner,” he says.

This Peacemaker spin-off was intended to feature Viola Davis reprising the Amanda Waller role, with several other Peacemaker alums also returning. However, the series “has had a couple of setbacks" according to Gunn. Safran added that "Waller has been a bumpy road," and the latest word is that the series is no longer in development.

Also no longer happening is a series about the lovably goofy Booster Gold . Booster Gold would've explored the character's impostor syndrome as he travels back in time and uses the technology of the future to make himself a present-day superhero.

Here's another one that has fallen by the wayside at the House of DC. While a new Wonder Woman movie isn't on the immediate horizon, DC was previously planning a TV series set on the island of Themyscira. Paradise Lost would've explore the origins and political intrigue of Diana's home. The series was billed as the DC equivalent of Game of Thrones.

Note: This story was updated on 8/19/2026 with the latest DC movie news. It was originally posted on 7/29/2021.

articles.title: Xbox’s ‘reset’: all the news about Microsoft’s layoffs and studio changes
articles.summary: Xbox boss Asha Sharma and chief content officer Matt Booty have warned of an Xbox “reset,” which is expected to include layoffs and studio closures.
articles.body: Xbox is making some big changes — again. On June 10th, a few months after Asha Sharma took over as CEO, she and newly promoted chief content officer Matt Booty sent a memo to staff warning of an “Xbox reset.” The business, they said, is facing significant challenges, including a 3 percent “accountability margin,” massively higher component prices for consoles due to the memory and storage shortage, and an “over extended” studio system. On July 6th, the company announced mass layoffs at Xbox as part of broader cuts across the company. About 1,600 staffers were laid off that day, with 1,600 more set to be cut over the course of Microsoft’s next fiscal year, Sharma said. South of Midnight developer Compulsion Games and Psychonauts creator Double Fine Productions will become independent again, while Senua developer Ninja Theory and State of Decay 3 maker Undead Labs will get new owners. In addition, management at Blade developer Arkane Studios is “beginning required consultation with its Works Council to review potential strategic options,” Sharma said. Sharma noted that there will also be changes at “Activision, Bethesda/ZeniMax, Blizzard, King, Mojang, and XBOX Game Studios” that will “vary in size.” That reportedly includes cutting around half of Doom developer id Software’s staff. Under Sharma’s leadership, Xbox has already made some other major changes, including upcoming price hikes for Xbox consoles, lowering Game Pass prices but cutting out new Call of Duty games, rebranding Xbox to XBOX, and making both Gears of War: E-Day and Clockwork Revolution Xbox console exclusives. Read on for all of our coverage of the shifts at Xbox.

articles.title: It Sounds Like Mike Flanagan Is Having a Tough Time Getting the Green Light on His Long-Awaited Dark Tower TV Series
articles.summary: Mike Flanagan has issued an update on his long-awaited The Dark Tower TV series, although it sounds like it’s still far from becoming a reality.
articles.body:
Mike Flanagan has issued an update on his long-awaited The Dark Tower TV series, although it sounds like it’s still far from becoming a reality.

Flanagan, famous for Netflix horror shows The Haunting of Hill House, The Haunting of Bly Manor, and Midnight Mass, has been trying to get an adaptation of Stephen King’s much-loved fantasy saga The Dark Tower off the ground for years, and while the script for Season 1 has King’s seal of approval, he’s struggling to get the go-ahead to start production on what he has described as his “Holy Grail” project.

The Dark Tower is currently “one of the most complicated properties to get started,” Flanagan told Entertainment Weekly . “Getting the green light on Dark Tower is a much longer and more involved process than anything else I’ve ever approached in my life.”

The Essentials: Stephen King's Dark Tower Multiverse

The priority for Flanagan is his Carrie TV show adaptation for Amazon’s Prime Video , which he developed as part of a multi-year deal he signed with the streamer earlier this year. The Dark Tower is not a part of the Amazon deal, although Flanagan has indicated that Prime Video could get behind it eventually. The big idea, Flanagan has said, is for five seasons of The Dark Tower followed by two standalone movies. But will they be made? That's the big question for fans, and, it seems, Flanagan himself.

Fans certainly hope Flanagan will get his chance to adapt The Dark Tower, especially after the 2017 movie, starring Idris Elba as Roland Deschain and Matthew McConaughey as his nemesis, Walter Padick, was panned by critics. Following the 2017 Nikolaj Arcel-directed feature adaptation, Flanagan said, “We can’t let that be the final word. We really can’t.”

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

articles.title: Archie Lives: We Review Every Title in Oni Press' Ambitious Archie Comics Reboot
articles.summary: We check out the first issues of all three of Oni Press' rebooted Archie comics and find that one series rises above the rest.
articles.body:
It’s been a while since we’ve run a proper comic book review on IGN, but that’s something I’m hoping to change in the months ahead. And what better time to get back in the habit than with Oni Press’ impending reboot of the Archie Comics line . In case you missed the news, Oni is launching a new wave of three comics that reinvent Archie and the Riverdale gang for a new generation. That includes the flagship Archie series as well as Sabrina the Teenage Witch and Archie in Hell.

To ring in this new era of comic book reviews on IGN, we figured the Archie reboot was the perfect starting point. We’ve been able to check out the first issue of all three series, and we’re here to render a verdict and let you know which, if any, are worth giving a look this fall.

We’re hoping to make new comic book reviews on IGN a regular thing again, so definitely head down to the comments and let us know what books you’d like to see us cover.

Creative Team: Writer Ben H. Winters & Artist Fábio Moon

This series is the obvious jumping-on point for most of the Archie-curious out there. It’s the classic Archie series reimagined for a new era. Though maybe “reimagined” is overselling things a bit. The new Archie doesn’t fundamentally rework the long-running series so much as it gives it a fresh coat of paint.

Which, for the most part, is just fine. The prospect of Casanova and Daytripper artist Fábio Moon getting the chance to work his magic on Riverdale was always the key selling point for me anyway, and in that regard the reboot doesn’t disappoint. Moon is basically the perfect artist to shoulder the burden of giving Archie Andrews a postmodern visual touch-up. His pages are free-flowing and dynamic and expertly capture the hectic nature of Archie’s overly busy day. Moon’s pencils and inks mesh well with Jason Wordie’s colors, which lend just the right sense of depth and texture to the art.

The main story featured in this issue offers a simple but largely effective gateway into Archie’s crazy little world. Riverdale High is holding a film festival, and Archie soon finds himself stretched thin as he tries to lend a helping hand to all of his friends while also pursuing his own big idea. The premise allows Winters and Moon to quickly cycle through the book’s major supporting cast and establish their various relationships with Archie, and it’s all done in an entertaining way.

The problem is mostly a lack of depth. The story is fun and lighthearted, but that’s about it. It doesn’t really strive to do anything that we wouldn’t have gotten out of a classic Archie Comics adventure. Give this same script to an artist like Dan Parent and it could just as easily be included in an Archie Double Digest in a grocery store checkout lane. Maybe I’m simply a victim of my own expectations, but I was hoping for something a little more experimental, or at least a story with more hints of a serialized narrative. For now, the previous “New Riverdale” reboot still stands as the more compelling example of reinventing Archie for the 21st century.

That said, Winters and Moon’s backup story does suggest the series is capable of a bit more. The backup focuses more on Jughead and digs a little deeper into the psychology of everyone’s favorite hamburger-scarfing best friend. Hopefully it’s a sign of more ambitious storytelling to come.

Creative Team: Writer Corinna Bechko & Artist Kano

If Archie #1 is guilty of playing things a little too safe and traditional, that’s not a problem for this reboot of its sister series. This is easily the most satisfying debut issue of the trio, one that strikes a nice balance between honoring the franchise’s wholesome, all-ages roots and embracing the possibilities of this new future.

Similar to Archie #1, Sabrina the Teenage Witch #1 enters Sabrina Spellman’s life at a particularly chaotic time. She’s just discovered her magical abilities and is trying to balance her newfound responsibilities with her desire to hang out with her friends and enjoy a good Halloween party. Bechko’s script wisely skips over the origin story for the most part, preferring to jump right in with what comes next.

While this issue also serves as an efficient debut for much of the book’s supporting cast, it’s really the dynamic between Sabrina and her cat Salem that steals the show. Salem is a lot of fun as he bickers with his befuddled owner, who’s still growing accustomed to the fact that her cat talks in the first place. In general, Sabrina comes across as very likable here, a girl torn between high school fun and the more urgent, darker world that’s just opened before her.

Kano’s art complements the lighthearted but slightly sinister vibe of the script quite well. Here, too, the series toes that line between honoring the past and establishing its own look and feel. Of particular note is Kano’s facial work, which is wonderfully expressive and helps give each character a welcome burst of personality. This is a book to keep an eye on.

Creative Team: Writer Patrick Horvath & Artist Tyler Crook

It was clear from the beginning that anyone who wanted to see a more subversive take on the Archie franchise with this Oni reboot would be best served with Archie in Hell. The series is very much the spiritual successor to Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa and Francesco Francavilla’s Afterlife with Archie , a book that boasted a fantastic premise but was undone by its unpredictable shipping schedule. Hopefully, that won’t be a problem this time around.

Probably the biggest selling point of Archie in Hell, apart from the basic appeal of infusing this universe with supernatural horror, is the fact that it’s written by Beneath the Trees Where Nobody Sees’ Patrick Horvath . A real match made in heaven there, even if the end result isn’t quite as strong out of the gate as I would have liked. Issue #1 is a bit of a slow burn, taking its sweet time to transition from the wholesome charm of a standard Archie adventure to something darker and more grotesque. It’s fun, but there’s not quite enough meat on this particular bone just yet.

The series also finds a fitting artist in horror comics veteran Tyler Crook. Crook and colorist Francesco Segala are adept at blending the old-school Archie aesthetic with a darker, more twisted vibe. Early on, you can almost trick yourself into believing you’re reading another straightforward Archie adventure, only to be reminded otherwise when the black magic and ritualistic sacrifices start unfolding on the page.

This series holds plenty of potential, but a lot is riding on the final page twist and where things go from there. It lacks the fast-paced start and easy “Night of the Living Dead in Riverdale” elevator pitch that Afterlife with Archie benefited from.

articles.title: After Obsession and Backrooms, It Ends Is the Latest Indie Horror-Thriller That Could
articles.summary: It Ends, the latest indie-horror-thriller-that-could, is both creepy and amusing thanks to its likable cast and filmmaker Alexander Ullom’s ability to exploit minimal resources to maximum effect.
articles.body:
It Ends will be released in select theaters on Friday, August 21, and enters wide release on August 28.

Remember that Talking Heads song “Road to Nowhere” ? It stars with these lyrics: “Well, we know where we're going / But we don't know where we've been” and “We're not little children / And we know what we want / And the future is certain / Give us time to work it out”...

It seems that David Byrne’s words are firmly entrenched in the minds of the team behind It Ends, the latest indie-horror-thriller-that-could, with its tale of a quartet of friends whose car trip turns into an existential joy ride on a never-ending road… a road to nowhere, you might say.

Written and directed (and edited) by newcomer Alexander Ullom, It Ends isn’t as outwardly cheery as the Talking Heads song sounds – it is a horror film after all – but it can be fun all the same. The four leads (Phinehas Yoon as James, Akira Jackson as Day, Noah Toth as Fisher, and Mitchell Cole as Tyler) have a playful banter that carries much of the film, particularly in its opening stretch where they innocently happen into what in another decade might’ve been an episode of Rod Serling ’s The Twilight Zone (or a Sartre play): The turn on the road they’re on never comes, and the group slowly realize they’re trapped on a paved nightmare, where if they dare stop the car for too long, raving maniacs emerge from the surrounding woods and engulf them. Their only choice? Drive, baby, drive. To continue the song analogies , these people may be on the road to purgatory, and they sure don't like the sound of that…

One question that always surrounds these tight-quarters movies is whether or not things can stay interesting, despite the film being set in one place. But rather than being limited by it, It Ends instead benefits from its contained setting. The first 15 minutes or so of It Ends are almost entirely shot in close-ups and two-shots of the cast inside the car as they chitter-chatter, happy to be reunited (Tyler hasn’t been on the scene recently but is back now that the other three are graduating from college). Even as the situation grows more concerning in that opening – where the heck is the exit off this road!? – Ullom’s camera remains restrained. The dude knows he’s got 90 minutes of movie to play out in this car and on the road outside it, and no place else, and he squeezes every bit that he can out of those settings. By the time Tyler and James exit to investigate the woods, the car’s flashing hazard lights cast an intermittent red glow where… wait… is that a face out there…? Did something just move behind that tree? And then BAM: The masses of lost souls or ghouls or whatever they are are upon our characters.

And that’s the thing about It Ends: The script allows for the characters to ask the same questions we’re asking while watching. These people who are appearing from out of the forest in a mania to overtake the car, begging to be let in, they’ve gotta be dead, right? Ghosts or shades of the living? Which means James and Tyler and Day and Fisher… well, maybe they’re dead too? Are they being punished for something they did in their “real” lives? The question is asked: Who in this car recently did something very, very bad, requiring karmic payback!? Speak up now!

So the questions and theories about what’s going on here are floated, particularly by James, the most driven and analytical of the group. But answers are a different story. Eventually the group settles into a sort of normalcy about their situation, driving and driving and driving. For a time, anyway.

Is the film about the road everyone finds themselves on as they enter adulthood? It Ends starts with the four talking about what’s next for them now that school is in the rearview mirror (if you will). Tyler, who’s already out in the real world as a working man, doesn’t seem particularly happy or satisfied with where life has taken him. James has given it all a lot of thought, and even has a job – and a selfie in his “first communion” work clothes – to prove it, but he doesn’t seem to be very happy either. Day’s living back home, and Fisher… is he just along for the ride? If he even has a plan for what’s next, I missed it.

Amid it all, these Gen Z kids are just hanging – yes, this is a hangout movie – and that’s a huge part of the appeal of the characters, and the film itself. Ullom has said he was partly inspired by Richard Linklater’s Slacker when making It Ends, and it shows, whether the group are debating who would win, a man with a gun or a man with 50 hawks, or contending with the monotony of living together in a car for weeks on end. (It must also be noted that Ullom shot most of this film on a mini Volume LED stage at his alma mater, Florida State, which is damned impressive.)

While never explicit in its intent, the film’s message is hard to shake. These four are trying to find their way in life, and as each comes to react to their situation in different ways, their fates seem to become increasingly sealed. And what is life in the real world if not a constant push to move forward? Do better, make more, get more, get there . Those people clawing at you as you pull away? Ignore them, they’re in the way, they’re the competition. Look, it’s a helluva job market out there, and I don’t make the rules – I just follow them. Talk about a horror show.

articles.title: 'We Just Have to Be Careful What We Pick': GTA 6 Won't Include Covid or Trump References That Could Become Dated, Rockstar Says
articles.summary: Rockstar has discussed the need to "be careful" with its satirical take on American culture in GTA 6, when asked about including references to recent events such as the Covid pandemic and Donald Trump's presidency.
articles.body:
Rockstar has discussed the need to "be careful" with its satirical take on American culture in GTA 6 , when asked about including references to recent events such as the Covid pandemic and Donald Trump's presidency.

Speaking to French outlet Trois Couleurs , Rockstar Games head of development Rob Nelson cited the "very long" development cycle of GTA 6 as a reason why Rockstar was cautious about what it parodies — to ensure things "stand the test of time."

"We develop on very long cycles," Nelson said. "The game's been in development since 2015, so the idea is gestating for a long time. The majority of the team really started rolling on to it after Red Dead Redemption 2 released in 2018.

"We have to be very careful about what ideas we choose to put in there, because it can take a long time to figure out what our angle is on this," he added. "Because by the time we write it and cast it and shoot it, and implement it, whatever it is – it could be gone, it could change, it could be dated. And so we're always trying to think about whether something will stand the test of time."

Nelson continued by stating that Rockstar was also only likely to pick elements that work with the story it wanted to tell and the world its characters inhabited. It's an interesting idea that, perhaps accurately, Jason and Lucia may just not care about some of the elements that players would consider emblematic of the U.S. today. They're criminals on the run, after all, and so likely have other things to worry about.

"I think there will always be things to satirise," Nelson continued, citing the "stupid challenges" undertaken by influencers and streamers. "There are always ridiculous situations and behaviours that we can find, but we just have to be careful about what we pick."

In a similar answer to the same question by The New York Times , Nelson insisted that Rockstar did not want "the risk of dating ourselves in a sort of awkward way," when Trump and Covid are mentioned. "So we have to look at things and go, What is going to have a timeless sort of quality that will speak very easily to relatable sort of human folly and foibles and will be remembered as part of this time?"

articles.title: GTA 6 Has ‘Big and Small Choices’ in Its Story, As Rockstar Takes Red Dead Redemption 2’s Player Agency to the Next Level
articles.summary: Rockstar took things to the next level with Red Dead Redemption 2’s story, and now it’s building on that for GTA 6’s story, which will feature “big and small choices” that impact Jason and Lucia’s journey.
articles.body:
It may be difficult to imagine now, but there was a time when people were disappointed that Red Dead Redemption's protagonist, John Marston, would not be leading Rockstar’s 2018 sequel. Arthur Morgan was an unknown, and it was somewhat unthinkable that he could mean more to anyone than the already established Marston.

Rockstar, of course, knew that would be the case. And so, during the production of Red Dead Redemption 2, it put a lot of careful thought into crafting Arthur’s tale, with the aim of ensuring Mr. Morgan could both connect with and reflect players better than even John had. And now, several years later, that same issue has been on Rockstar’s mind while creating GTA 6 protagonists, Jason and Lucia.

“One of the things we are interested in exploring with these games – and it’s something we did probably most consciously on Red Dead Redemption 2 – is the idea of how much of this character is them and how much of it is you, the player?” says Rob Nelson, Rockstar North’s co-studio head.

We spoke with Nelson as part of a recent visit to Rockstar North, and he told us about how important it is for player agency and choices, both “big and small” to permeate through the studio’s stories and the characters at the centre of them.

GTA 6 Vintage Vice City Pack Screenshots

“For example, Arthur – as we played through Red Dead Redemption 2, sometimes it felt like ‘Why am I listening to Dutch?’ He's clearly crazy,” says Nelson. “You know – ‘Why am I helping these people? I don’t even know them.’

“People would ask us that, and we would say, ‘Well, because Dutch saved you when you were 15 years old, when you didn't know how to read.’ And they say, ‘Me? He Saved Arthur.’ So, we tried to do a couple of things to address this. We added an element to the story where Dutch is the only one who knows where Arthur’s money – and all the gang’s money – is, to try to create a secondary, more player-centric motivation.”

“So, if it was not enough for you as the player to just take Arthur's loyalty to Dutch at face value and go along with it, we'll also try and give you a personal reason as the player to be invested for your own sense of wanting something for you,” Nelson concluded.

One way you could build stronger bonds within the world of Red Dead Redemption 2 was to spend time at camp and talk to each member of the Van Der Linde gang. While a great many games feature conversation between the player’s character and NPCs, RDR2’s dialogue system supported both narrative-driven chats and incidental small talk, the latter of which contributed to the camp’s truly authentic atmosphere. This is something that Rockstar also aims to carry over into GTA 6, with Jason and Lucia’s safehouses across the fictional state of Leonida operating more like the interactable camps of the Wild West than traditional Grand Theft Auto homes have done. It’s a continuation of Red Dead Redemption 2’s commitment to characters leading the studio’s stories.

“We needed to make sure we had missions where you spent time with each member of the gang to try and get to know them to help the player form a connection with them,” explains Nelson.

“Another thing we tried to do to enhance the player’s connection to their character in that game involved any of the kind acts that Arthur was able to perform,” he continued. “Originally, many of them were mandatory, but that felt wrong. So, we started taking them off the main story flow and just making them optional. So, you as a player were required to go and meet his ex-girlfriend, Mary Linton, but you didn't have to help get her little brother out of the cult, and you didn’t ever have to meet her again.

“We tried to make sure that a lot of these things were optional so that, hopefully, if you wanted Arthur to have some sort of redemption arc, you felt more strongly connected to it because you helped him achieve it as a player,” Nelson adds.

That feeling of shaping your own Arthur and deciding which end of the honor meter he ended up at is a masterstroke of open world storytelling. It makes every action count, from small-time theft to life-or-death decision-making. Again, it’s something Rockstar is looking to build on in GTA 6, with its equivalent of the honor system, Jason and Lucia’s Criminal Profiles, changing depending on the outcome of every choice, big and small. This, alongside how you choose to make them bond romantically, will affect the story, much like how Red Dead 2’s would change in specific moments, such as whether a prowling wolf or peaceful deer appears in Arthur’s dreams.

“We also made very subtle changes to the cutscenes and [Arthur’s] stated motivations for things”, Nelson explained. “If you were high honor and if you as the player had been showing that you cared about these things, Arthur would tell John, ‘Get out of here when this is going down. Do it for me; it would make me feel...good, I guess.’ But if you had low honor, he didn’t say that. He said, ‘Don’t be an idiot’. And it wasn’t black hat versus white hat – it was just figuring out how to not make Arthur too sentimental, if that was not the way you were playing.”

Every Detail in the GTA 6 Cover Art Explained

“Interestingly, some people would get the low honor ending that resulted in Micah shooting Arthur in the head, and they would die face down in the dirt, and they’d say, ‘Why did that happen to me?’” Nelson laughs.

We don’t yet know how many different endings GTA 6’s story may have, or how drastically it can change depending on the state of Jason and Lucia’s relationship and their Criminal Profiles. It certainly seems like we’ll need to spend plenty of time outside of those main missions in order to make their bond with each other, and in turn, our bond with them, ring true.

“There are lots of choices, big and small. The small ones add up to mean something, some big ones mean a lot in the moment you make them,” reveals Nelson.

“It’s interesting to play around with and explore these ideas, and we are definitely continuing down this path with GTA 6,” he continues. “With the relationship, we start Jason and Lucia off wanting to give it a shot, but just going through the story and playing missions together may not be enough to keep them together. You’ll have to keep them together by spending a bit of time together in the open world, and then hopefully that will reinforce your connection to them and increase your investment in their story.”

Simon Cardy is a Senior Editor at IGN who can mainly be found skulking around open world games, indulging in Korean cinema, or despairing at the state of Tottenham Hotspur and the New York Jets. Follow him on Bluesky at @cardy.bsky.social .

articles.title: Rockstar Snuck Red Dead Redemption 2 Into Its GTA 6 Extended Look — And Of Course, Fans Spotted It Immediately
articles.summary: Did you spot the world of Red Dead Redemption 2 in last night's GTA 6 Extended Look? Rockstar's cowboy epic made a brief appearance — and, of course, some fans spotted it immediately.
articles.body:
Did you spot the world of Red Dead Redemption 2 in last night's Grand Theft Auto 6 Extended Look? Rockstar's cowboy epic made a brief appearance — and, of course, some GTA 6 fans spotted it immediately.

During a TV commercial for what might be the unhealthiest burger ever invented, a lush outdoor scene features in the background. A winding river courses through green trees, with several notable rock formations on its banks. Adorning the scene are an array of animals — which will presumably soon be turned into the burger's 30,000 calorie contents.

Even more excitingly for Rockstar's fans, however, this was clearly footage taken within Red Dead Redemption 2, and players rushed to reach the exact spot. There's no array of animals here normally, and clearly Rockstar has made a couple of tweaks with its lighting. But the river is the same, as are the trees and most of the rocks. It's a fun Easter egg for fans of the developer's previous game, now looking forward to its next.

If you want to visit it yourself, reddit user DangerousLeo (who found the exact spot) has highlighted the U-bend in the Kamassa River, north-west of Annesburg, just to the west of Deer Cottage. (How did DangerousLeo find the location so quickly? Well, they admit to having more than 730 hours logged on Red Dead Redemption 2 to date.)

So, Red Dead Redemption 2 4K remaster confirmed? Not quite. It's likely Rockstar tweaked a version of its previous game simply for this in-game commercial, with the pre-existing location a handy substitute for using GTA 6's open world, which has likely kept changing through development.

articles.title: Everything We Learnt about Silver Palace at gamescom
articles.body:
Following the conclusion of its recent beta test, and with over 10-million pre registrations made globally in the run-up to gamescom, developer and publisher Elementa debuted a new trailer for open-world action RPG, Silver Palace, at gamescom’s prestigious Opening Night Live.

In development for PC, mobile and⁠ – in a surprising reveal⁠ – the official announcement that it’s coming to PlayStation 5, IGN was on the ground at gamescom to check out the Silver Palace booth. If you’ve not seen the trailer yet, you can watch it now, below:

The trailer opens with a spooky looking operating room as a doctor examines a corpse made of Silverium, before shifting to a sprawling city filled with winding streets ⁠– and our first look at the protagonist of Silver Palace, the Detective. The trailer then follows the Detective as they carry out their investigation, engage in combat and explore the city. Glimpses of characters Ashley, Gratia and Red Rose, boss encounters and the operating room showcase the game’s mix of dynamic combat and tension. After the corpse suddenly fractures and sends shimmering silver droplets everywhere, the trailer unveils the brand-new multiplayer combat experience called “House of Greed”.

At the booth, as you’d expect, we had the obligatory photo spot and merchandise zones, but there was also a playable demo area where we got to get our hands on Silver Palace proper. With support for DLSS 4.5 and Raytracing at launch, the NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 PCs they had on-site gave them a chance to show off just how immersive the world of Silvernia will be.

During our hands-on with the demo we were introduced to a mystical world filled with flying silver whales, ornate buildings and fantastical enemies. After a failed assassination attempt on the Queen, the protagonist ⁠– the Detective ⁠– is quickly forced into a boss battle between two huge humanoids emerging from a portal. Combat flowed between light, ranged and ultimate attacks, with dodges and parries helping you avoid damage while keeping the pressure on the enemy. After a spot of exploration in the city of Silvernia on a silverwork horse, we were thrust into another boss encounter, this time against ‘Cinderella’ ⁠– except this version used her horse-drawn pumpkin carriage as a weapon rather than a means to travel to a royal ball. Here we got a taste of the other playable characters who seamlessly switch in and out of combat, each providing a unique moveset and extravagant ultimate ability.

Multiple live stage performances, cosplayer meet and greets and influencer sessions with iCrimax, HoneyPuu and more gave fans plenty of immersive opportunities where they engaged not only with the game but significant figures in the scene. Characters portrayed included the Detective, Alf, Red Rose amongst several other significant figures, and the game’s pumpkin carriage from the Cinderella Boss Battle was brought to life in stunning fashion with an impressive sculpture. Live band performances and dance showcases at the booth brought the energy to Hall 6 and, for those who took part in activities surrounding their presence, there was a healthy host of rewards such as art cards, blind-box coaster sets, and a very nicely put together “Detective set”.

We also spent some time with the game’s development team at their booth in Cologne, to have a chat about things in a bit more detail. Here’s what they had to say:

IGN: Your ONL trailer has a noticeably darker, more horror-inspired tone, and some viewers may even be reminded of franchises like Resident Evil. This feels quite different from the main tone of Silver Palace. Was that contrast intentional?

Yes. For this trailer, we intentionally adopted a light horror-inspired editing style, so we understand why some viewers may draw comparisons to well-known horror titles. What we really wanted to highlight, however, was the contrast between Silver Palace’s elegant, fairy-tale-inspired characters and the distorted, unsettling creatures featured in the trailer. That contrast creates a very different atmosphere while still remaining rooted in the world of Silver Palace.

The ONL trailer also teased what looks like a new gameplay mode. Can you tell us more about it?

Yes. The mode, titled House of Greed, is still in an early stage of development and is planned as part of the main game experience. It is designed as a multiplayer mode and uses a classic over-the-shoulder camera and related character-control systems, with a stronger focus on room-based exploration and third-person shooting. The experience is quite different from the main game’s action combat, which centers around a four-character squad and real-time character switching.

You recently passed the huge milestone of 10 million pre-registrations. Is there anything you would like to say to the many players out there who are patiently waiting for Silver Palace?

We received a great deal of valuable feedback from players during both CBT1 and CBT2, and those comments have been extremely important to the entire Silver Palace development team. We’re very grateful to everyone who has been following the game and waiting patiently for its release.

articles.title: Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy's Game Director and Star on Why Sophia Is So Special and Why This Prequel Let the Team 'Get Some Fresh Air' | gamescom 2026
articles.summary: Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy has just been released on PS5, Xbox Series X/S, and PC, and we had the chance at gamescom to speak to David Dedeine, co-founder of Asobo and game director, and Anna Demetriou, Sophia's voice actor, about this big moment for the franchise.
articles.body:
Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy has just been released on PS5, Xbox Series X/S, and PC, and we had the chance at gamescom to speak to David Dedeine, co-founder of Asobo and game director, and Anna Demetriou, Sophia's voice actor, about this big moment for the franchise.

The story being told in Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy is a prequel that centers on Sophia and her journey to the Minotaur's island to confront a mythical creature at the heart of a devastating curse. It's an emotional tale not only for the players, but for Demetriou herself.

"I think sometimes in the acting world, there's a phrase of a character being on center or off center for whoever is playing them," Demetriou said. "For me, Sophia is very much on center. She feels very close to me. This means it hasn't been so much of a stretch to access her or play her. I think we've also delved into her backstory and, as you leave Resonance and you sit in what that game shows you, it makes sense in how you are then led to the Requiem version of her. If there was never anything again, to me, she makes sense and is complete."

Demetriou, after revealing that Just Cause was an important title that helped welcome her into the world of games, said she brought a lot of herself to Sophia and had a great relationship with Resonance's lead writer, Carol Ann Bañuls.

"What was actually really nice on [Resonance] and quite a unique experience was that the person who had originally written Sophia's character in A Plague Tale: Requiem was not the one writing on Resonance," Demetriou said. "We had the amazing Carol Ann Bañuls on this one, who I got on with so well professionally and personally. It all felt very naturally collaborative as I'd already played this character and she was coming to it new.

"This led to a lot of moments of us saying, 'Okay, how can we blend what I know about this character already and what you're bringing to this character that's new and makes something fresh with it together?' She was also so open to, 'Do you like this line? Do you think that she would say something like this?' And I would say, 'Yeah, I like it too!' Or, 'How about we try twisting it, and maybe try this instead?' And she was always up for it. I don't always have that creative freedom as an actor, so it was nice to feel that we got to do this together a lot of the time."

We then chatted with Dedeine about this new story and how it being a prequel offered some interesting challenges.

"There are a lot of different dimensions on this because did not want to disappoint people, as we knew since the beginning that Amicia and Hugo were gone," Dedeine said. "It was not possible to continue on the same vein, and we knew that if we tried to mimic what we did in the past, it would definitely be a wrong move.

"Even in A Plague Tale: Requiem, when we decided to go for the ending we chose, we knew it was the end for a lot of things. So for this, we wanted to open the window a little bit, get some fresh air, and change a little bit the tone too because it's seven years in a row that we've been walking in this universe. However, that concept is a bit complicated because you need to redefine things, and sometimes you fall back too easily on the existing rail and sometimes you try to go too far in the other direction. I think that was the trickiest part, finding this balance between adding the right amount of new flavor while keeping the spirit and the tone we had in the previous games."

One of the biggest changes in this game compared to the previous one is the absence of the iconic swarms of rats. Dedeine assures fans that they shouldn't be worried, because something just as sinister has taken their place.

"There is something very special that replaces the rats, and in a much more dynamic way," Dedeine said. "It's also something we haven't shown because we want to keep it a big surprise, but I think it's something interesting and innovative. I'm curious to see how people are going to react."

Speaking of players reacting, that is happening right now as Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy is now available on PS5, Xbox Series X/S, and PC. In our review, we said it is a "prequel spinoff that takes a lot of interesting chances with the series, following a new protagonist, refocusing its encounters around melee combat, and even introducing a whole new way to haunt your dreams."

articles.title: What Console Should You Buy for GTA 6? We Break Down PS5 vs. Xbox Pricing, Deals, and More
articles.summary: What is the best console to play Grand Theft Auto 6 on? We break down PS5, PS5 Pro, and Xbox Series X pricing, expected frame rates, and new or upcoming hardware deals, alongside whether it's worth waiting for a PC release.
articles.body:
Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally starting to feel real. After years of trailers, delays, rumours, and more leaks than Rockstar Games would probably care to count, we've now had our best look at the game yet, thanks to the extended look trailer , alongside our dedicated GTA 6 preview right here on IGN .

And now, finally, it's just a matter of months before we can actually play it. GTA 6 launches on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S on November 19, 2026, with pre-load beginning on November 12 .

But there's still one pretty important question to answer: which console should you actually use to play GTA 6? And should you even buy a console for it, or simply wait for the inevitable PC release instead?

$100 PlayStation Store Gift Card [Digital Code]

Grand Theft Auto 6 - Ultimate Edition (Digital)

Grand Theft Auto 6 - PS5 Physical (Code in Box)

Grand Theft Auto 6 - Xbox Physical (Code in Box)

Grand Theft Auto 6 - Ultimate Edition Upgrade

Look, there's no doubt that the vast majority of players will end up playing GTA 6 on PS5 . Sony's console has a sizeable lead over Xbox Series X|S, with around 95 million PS5 consoles sold , compared with an estimated 35 million Xbox Series X|S consoles .

But it's not quite as simple as saying, "play it on PS5, like everyone else."

For starters, plenty of people still haven't made the jump to the current generation. If you're still playing on PS4 or Xbox One, GTA 6 could well be the game that finally convinces you to upgrade. Unfortunately, you couldn't have picked a much more expensive time to do it, with console prices, games, storage, and just about everything else seemingly getting pricier by the minute. It's a sign of the times, I'm afraid.

Rockstar has also yet to confirm the game's frame-rate targets , but current expectations point towards 30fps on the standard PS5 and Xbox Series X . That's hardly surprising given the sheer scale and visual ambition of GTA 6, but it does raise an interesting question about the PS5 Pro.

The Pro has considerably more horsepower than the standard PS5, along with PSSR upscaling, so you'd expect it to have an advantage. Whether that advantage will be enough to push GTA 6 to 60fps, however, is another matter entirely.

I'd be more surprised if the PS5 Pro didn't offer some kind of visual or performance advantage, but I'd be very wary of buying one on the assumption that it will deliver a locked 60fps. Until Rockstar confirms its performance targets, that's simply not something anyone can guarantee.

That being said, if you forced me to give an answer, the PS5 Pro is still probably going to be top option for getting the best performance for GTA 6. If only it wasn't so horrendously expensive.

If you don't already own a PS5 or Xbox Series X|S , GTA 6 presents a slightly awkward conundrum. On the one hand, this is arguably the biggest game release of the generation, and you're probably going to want to play it as soon as it arrives. On the other, buying an entire console for one game is an increasingly expensive proposition in 2026.

Sony's current US prices put the PS5 Digital Edition at $599.99 , the standard PS5 with a disc drive at $649.99 , and the PS5 Pro at a frankly eye-watering $899.99 . Microsoft isn't doing much better, with the Xbox Series S now costing $499.99 and the Xbox Series X reaching $749.99 for the digital model or $799.99 with a disc drive. Yikes.

PlayStation 5 825GB Console - Digital Edition

Yet, somehow, despite these bonkers prices, there's somehow also an argument for buying sooner rather than later. Console prices have been consistently heading in the wrong direction, and the broader component shortage isn't exactly helping. Major retailers have already warned that console stock could struggle to keep up with demand over the holiday period, with one senior games buyer claiming retailers have been told they won't receive the number of consoles they want ahead of GTA 6's launch.

That's not exactly a guarantee that you'll be fighting scalpers for a PS5 come November, though. Sony insists it has secured enough memory to hit its PS5 sales target for the financial year, despite the ongoing component difficulties. Yet, with GTA 6 expected to drive a huge upgrade cycle, I'd rather have my console sorted well before November 19 than find myself scrambling for one at the last minute.

Still, if you can, I would still avoid rushing out and paying full price for a console simply because GTA 6 is coming. If you're starting from scratch, keep an eye out for bundles, retailer promotions, trade-in offers, and, particularly as we get closer to November, any GTA 6-specific console deals that might appear.

The Best PS5 and Xbox Console Deals Right Now

Free $50 Best Buy Gift Card with GTA 6 + Console Purchase

Speaking of console deals. While it's slim pickings out there, there are still some potentially decent offers to consider in the run-up to GTA 6's launch.

Top of the list right now is Best Buy, with the retailer offering a $50 reward certificate to anyone who bundles a Grand Theft Auto 6 preorder with an eligible PlayStation 5 or Xbox console .

That's not a bad offer, particularly if you go for the refurbished PS5 at $539.99 . You're effectively getting $110 off the current $649.99 price of a new disc-drive PS5, plus another $50 in Best Buy credit to put towards a future purchase. Just bear in mind that this is the original 2020 PS5 model, complete with its 825GB SSD, rather than the newer, slimmer 1TB model.

And honestly, refurbished is where I'd be looking right now if you're trying to keep the cost of getting GTA 6-ready as low as possible. You're not going to get much of a discount on brand-new PS5 hardware at the moment, so a reputable refurbished model can make considerably more sense.

That's why the next deal I'd consider is a certified refurbished PS5 directly from PlayStation through the PS Direct store . A refurbished PS5 is currently $549, while the refurbished PS5 Digital Edition is $499.

That makes the choice between Best Buy and PlayStation a little more interesting. For just $9 more, the PS Direct option gets you the newer PS5 design with 1TB of storage, although you'll be giving up Best Buy's $50 reward certificate. If you're happy with digital games, the $499 refurbished PS5 Digital Edition is arguably the most compelling option of the lot, particularly if GTA 6 is the main reason you're buying a console in the first place .

PlayStation 5 - Digital Edition 1TB - Certified Refurbished

Sony has also announced plans to stop producing physical game discs for new PlayStation releases from January 2028, meaning we're potentially looking at the final few years of physical PlayStation gaming.

That doesn't mean your existing discs suddenly become useless, or that physical games are disappearing overnight, but it does make the $50 saving on a Digital Edition a little more tempting if you're starting from scratch and don't have an existing physical library.

I'd still recommend thinking carefully before going all-in on digital, though. The disc-drive PS5 gives you access to used games, physical discounts, borrowing and reselling games, so that extra $50 isn't necessarily money wasted. But if you have no existing physical library and are comfortable buying digitally, saving that money upfront is certainly a tempting proposition.

There's one more date worth keeping in mind if you're thinking about buying a console for GTA 6: Black Friday .

GTA 6 is currently scheduled to launch on November 19, just over a week before Black Friday officially arrives on November 27. But don't take that to mean you'll have to wait until November 27 to find a deal. Black Friday has long since evolved beyond a single day, with major retailers typically launching their sales days or sometimes even weeks in advance.

For example, PlayStation ran their Black Friday sale from November 21-29 last year, with Black Friday proper on Nov. 28, that means they kicked things off a week prior. I'd expect something similar for this year (around Nov. 19-20), or perhaps even earlier to help drive up console sales ready for GTA 6.

PS5 consoles received a $100 discount last year , which, if repeated, would be your best opportunity to save at least something.

For those who didn't take advantage, look away now, but this actually brought PS5 Pro consoles down to $649.99 ($749.99 --> $649.99), while the console now retails for $899.99 in the US after price hikes earlier this year. It was also $399.99 for the PS5 Digital Edition (now up to $599.99), and $449.99 for the PS5 Disc Edition (now up to $649.99). Ouch!

If the $100 price cut is repeated this year, you'd be looking at $799.99 for the PS5 Pro , $549.99 for the PS5 Disc Edition , and $499.99 for the Digital Edition .

Fingers crossed, I guess? Discounts for this year aren't necessarily guaranteed either. The recent PlayStation Days of Play sale brought with it zero console deals, despite them usually being a pretty major part of it.

Therefore, while I'd absolutely keep Black Friday on your radar, I wouldn't blindly wait for it. If anything, I'd probably recommend sticking with, as I mentioned, a refurbished PS5 deal while they are regularly available.

PlayStation 5 - 1TB - Certified Refurbished

Do You Even Need a Console to Play GTA 6?

Right now, yes. There is no PC version of GTA 6. That doesn't mean there won't be one, though. Rockstar has a long history of bringing its biggest games to PC after their initial console releases, so waiting is a perfectly reasonable option if you already have a capable gaming PC.

The catch, of course, is that we have absolutely no idea when that PC version will arrive. It could be a year later, it could be considerably longer, and Rockstar hasn't committed to one at all yet.

If you desperately want to play GTA 6 on launch day, waiting for PC isn't really an option. If you're perfectly happy to wait, however, spending up to $900 on a console you otherwise wouldn't have bought becomes much harder to justify.

GTA 6 Reveal: 15 New Screenshots, Including 1 Exclusive on IGN

On the topic of GTA 6 on PC, IGN's Jacqueline Thomas also recently wrote : "The only problem is that it was running on a base PS5 . The game looks incredible regardless, but there were certainly moments where the frame rate slowed down considerably."

"I had already heard word that GTA 6 will only get a 60fps mode on the PS5 Pro , and now I can definitely see why. With all those lighting effects and the high-resolution textures, Grand Theft Auto 6 is really going to make the base consoles chug ."

"I have a hard time believing that GTA 6 will even be able to run at a steady 60fps on even the PS5 Pro, even though I know just how talented Rockstar's engineers are at making gorgeous games run on limited hardware. What I really want to do is take away those limits with an extemely powerful graphics card ."

I mean, never say never? But also, no, I find this unlikely to happen in the near future... Unless? No, no, you can't convince me otherwise. GTA 6 is not coming to Nintendo Switch 2.

We visited Rockstar North to see GTA 6 and came away seriously impressed by a live gameplay demo . The 30-minute play session showcased a Grand Theft Auto with a huge emphasis on the little details that make an open world feel like a real place.

We spoke to Rob Nelson, co-studio head of Rockstar North, to learn about how GTA 6 is building on the series’ almost 30-year legacy: “It’s a Step Forward in All Respects.”

Across both the new “Extended Look” video and the demo session we saw at Rockstar, we’ve learned many new gameplay details .

GTA 6 will feature ‘a Very Big Map’ that’s home to its most complex world yet.

That world features the same style of satirical humour GTA is historically known for, but Rockstar admits it has to be “careful” with its jokes .

The developer considered four protagonists for GTA 6 before settling on a criminal couple.

Jason and Lucia’s Bonnie and Clyde-style romance is optional , and can be played more like a platonic partnership.

With over a decade of anticipation, Rockstar is “nervous” about the pressure to deliver .

The new wanted level system adds deeper complexity to GTA 6’s police chases.

Car jacking has been significantly upgraded , with luxury vehicles featuring advanced security systems and electronic keys that must be cloned.

articles.title: Making Exorcist II Was Hell on Earth, and This New Documentary About Director John Boorman Proves It
articles.summary: Review: John Boorman and the Devil is a fun and engrossing look at the creation of what is considered to be one of the worst sequels ever made.
articles.body:
Boorman and the Devil will be released in New York City on August 28 before expanding to other cities on September 4.

“A dream to some… a nightmare to others!”

That line, spoken by Merlin in director John Boorman’s 1981 epic Excalibur , could very well describe the filmmaker’s experience while making Exorcist II: The Heretic , the disastrous 1977 sequel to William Friedkin’s landmark horror original. Reviled by critics, laughed at by audiences, and nearly career-ending for Boorman, Exorcist II became a cautionary tale in Hollywood about the dangers of too much of a good thing. And now, a documentary about the making of the film has been released, and it’s an engrossing look at the art of filmmaking and the tension between artist and audience.

Directed by David Kittredge, Boorman and the Devil traces where John Boorman was prior to taking on Exorcist II (namely, having just suffered through another career lowpoint with the oddball sci-fi film Zardoz ) before digging in on the writing, production – including an extended hiatus during which the filmmaker was gravely ill and in the hospital – and eventual release and self-destruction of the film while the Hollywood Eye of Sauron looked on. As a matter of fact, it was during that period that Boorman, who took most of the blame for the film’s reception, said in an interview, “What do you want me to do, immolate myself on Hollywood Boulevard?”

The documentary is buoyed by interviews with key players behind the film, including a reflective Boorman himself and stars Linda Blair and the late Louise Fletcher, while commentary is also offered by various crew members who worked on the picture, film critics, and filmmakers alike, the latter of which includes, kind of randomly, Joe Dante and Karyn Kusama, and less randomly, current horror icon Mike Flanagan, who's working on his own take on The Exorcist for next year, The Exorcist: Martyrs .

Boorman, who is 93 now but apparently shot his interview for Kittredge about seven years ago, is sharp and dryly funny as he looks back at the ups and downs of not just Exorcist II – which he would rather have just been called The Heretic, as he never saw the film as a sequel as much as a “riposte” to the original – but also of his life as a filmmaker. “I've often felt that I've been braver in my filmmaking, and more cowardly in my life,” he says. “Perhaps there's only so much bravery you can muster, and I've put mine into the films.”

Certainly, his intention with – and let’s observe the master’s wishes from here on out and just call the film by the name he’d prefer – The Heretic was noble and brave. He recalls how, in the wake of his film Deliverance ’s huge success, he passed on directing the original Exorcist because, after reading the book on which it was based, he determined that it was about “torturing a child.” But by the time The Heretic came about, Boorman was licking his wounds after Zardoz and trying to get the project that would eventually become Excalibur off the ground. The two-page treatment that the studio provided him had hints of a metaphysical approach to the material that intrigued the director. As he told Max von Sydow when trying to get the actor to return for the sequel, the film would be “a beautiful poetic healing film bearing the hope of spiritual regeneration.”

And so he signed on to the project. Though in doing so, as he himself admits here, Boorman miscalculated what kind of film this needed to be. He may have been making The Heretic, but audiences were expecting Exorcist II. And that is where things truly went wrong.

Boorman and the Devil drags just a tad in its first chunk as it recounts the story we’ve all heard before about the sunsetting of traditional Hollywood studio films and the rise of New Hollywood, plus some time spent on the state of sequels back then (they were more Beneath the Planet of the Apes than The Empire Strikes Back at that time) and Boorman’s career. Perhaps part of the problem here is that these days it’s that much harder to differentiate a feature-length documentary from, well, a YouTube essay. Kittredge steers clear of that danger in part through his use of some slick illustrations and animation which depict behind-the-scenes events, often in comic fashion. And fortunately, once the doc gets into the guts of how The Heretic was made, as told by the people who made it – and how it went horribly wrong – the agony and the ecstasy of the project comes to life.

Louise Fletcher, who passed away in 2022, is a hoot as she recounts her time on the production, having essentially replaced Ellen Burstyn (who refused to return after the difficult production of the first film) as the adult female lead, albeit in a different role. The One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest actress (though she’ll always be Kai Winn to me) regularly has a zinger ready as she reflects on her Heretic time, like when she laughs that she “would’ve been better in the first one!” Meanwhile, un-credited co-writer, second-unit director, and “creative associate” Rospo Pallenberg, who was a frequent collaborator of Boorman’s, is also present and accounted for here, even as he’s painted as something of a villain, or at the very least, an unwanted presence by Linda Blair, among others.

Full of interesting and often funny anecdotes, as well as some scary ones – too many people wound up in the hospital while making this film! – in the end, Boorman and the Devil is about the filmmaker and his own personal devil, which is figuring out how to make his art while also satisfying the masters who pay for it – not just the studio, but the audience as well. We know he found that balance eventually, but making The Heretic almost finished him off for good.

articles.title: Jeremy Renner Teases Hawkeye Return as Avengers: Doomsday Reshoots Reportedly Underway
articles.summary: Hawkeye star Jeremy Renner appears to be teasing a long-awaited return to the MCU, as a final round of Avengers: Doomsday reshoots reportedly gets underway.
articles.body:
Hawkeye star Jeremy Renner appears to be teasing a long-awaited return to the MCU, as a final round of Avengers: Doomsday reshoots reportedly gets underway.

Renner posted what appeared to be a clear tease for his involvement via Instagram today, with a photo of his Hawkeye costume set to the "Hawkeye Theme" music.

The timing of this post is very interesting, as it follows confirmation this week from M'Baku actor Winston Duke, who stated that "additional photography for Avengers: Doomsday" is now underway, per an interview with CNA .

Of course, Avengers: Doomsday is now just four months from launch — meaning that any additional material shot now has a just limited time to be worked into the production. But Marvel seems to have planned for this situation, with filming essentially tacked on to the start of filming for 2027's Avengers: Secret Wars, which is expected to begin its own production shoot in September.

Indeed, it's likely that any additional work on Doomsday at this stage will be for shorter scenes or smaller moments, rather than any major alterations to Doomsday's plot. Comments from Marvel tipster Daniel Richtman , who has a decent track record reporting MCU leaks, suggest that this filming will be used to "add a lot of cameos" — of which OG Avenger Hawkeye is presumably one.

After appearances in numerous MCU films, audiences last saw Renner as Hawkeye in the enjoyable Disney+ TV series of the same name, where he mentored Hailee Steinfeld's Kate Bishop and saved the day just in time for Christmas. Since then, Renner has been recovering from injuries sustained during his serious snowplough accident in January 2023, and said he had turned down a subsequent offer to return for a second season of Hawkeye due to a disagreement with Disney over pay.

The Most Surprising Avengers and Marvel Characters Not Announced for Doomsday

"They asked me to do Season 2, and they offered me half the money. I’m like, ‘Well, it’s going to take me twice the amount of work for half the amount of money, and eight months of my time, essentially, to do it for half the amount," Renner claimed.

"I'm like, 'I'm sorry? Why? Did you think I’m only half the Jeremy because I got ran over? Maybe that's why you want to pay me half of what I made on the first season.' This is not Marvel, mind you. This is like, just Disney, not even really Disney. It’s just the penny pinchers, the accountants. I told them to go fly a kite. I mean, just at the insult offer. So we didn’t see eye to eye on it."

Thankfully, Renner suggested he was still open to appearing as Hawkeye again, just not in those circumstances. And now, it seems, we may get one more appearance from the Avengers' best archer, at least.

Avengers: Doomsday is finally set to arrive in theaters on December 18, and even without Renner and the addition of further cameos, boasts one of the most stacked movie casts of all time. Fan interest and excitement for Avengers: Doomsday has been strong, with ticket pre-sales shifting faster than those for Spider-Man: Brand New Day . Looking for more ways to get ready? Despite saying that Avengers: Doomsday would reset the MCU to 'Phase Zero' , Marvel has released a watchlist of 15 movies and TV shows you should watch before Avengers: Doomsday rolls around .
