articles.title: Train to Busan Director Yeon Sang-ho Attempts to Reclaim the Zombie King Crown With Colony, But a Shallow Script Trips Up These Ghouls
articles.summary: Colony review: This is no Train to Busan.
articles.body:
When Train to Busan — Yeon Sang-ho’s taut KTX-set thriller about a girl dad’s (Gong Yoo) desperate quest to keep his daughter (Kim Su-an) safe in a burgeoning zombie apocalypse — was released in 2016, it became one of the first South Korean films to break through to a global mainstream audience. A decade later, the statuses of both the zombie genre and Korean pop culture in the West have evolved.

General audiences have mostly moved on from the zombie craze of the 2000s and 2010s, a diminishing interest no doubt partially fueled by oversaturation as well as by a global pandemic that made virus-related stories way less fun to watch. And Korean media is no longer niche in the U.S.; the East Asian country is currently producing some of the most popular stories in the world. 2022’s All of Us Are Dead , a zombie outbreak series set in a Korean high school, became one of Netflix’s most-watched series ever , proving that there’s still a hunger for zombie stories that hit on societal anxiety with brutal precision . Unfortunately, Colony does not.

It must be annoying for Yeon, whose explorations of society-level psychological horror have evolved in projects like Hellbound (2021-2024) and Revelations (2025), to constantly have critics and audiences compare his every project — often unfavorably — to that breakout film. But that’s the curse one must bear when you make a modern horror classic, and when it comes to Colony — which, unlike animated prequel short Seoul Station (2016) and live-action sequel Peninsula (2020), is his first original zombie tale in a decade — it feels particularly inevitable.

Nearly 60 years into the modern zombie movie, it’s difficult to do anything original. Colony finds its glimpses of originality in the construction of its zombie virus… which isn’t a virus at all, but rather a mold-based biotech weapon designed to eliminate those messy barriers between humans. In the mind of disgruntled and incredibly ambitious scientist Seo Young-cheol (gleefully played by Koo Kyo-hwan), miscommunication is the source of human suffering. His solution? To create a slime mold that binds us all together as one hivemind-like consciousness.

Seo unleashes the virus at a conference for his former company, Chains Bio, by injecting the slime mold directly into the veins of Kang Woo-chul, the CEO who fired Seo for his maniacal interests but kept using his research to bulk up his bottom line. From there, the virus quickly spreads across the multi-building, high-rise department store where the biotech presentation is taking place. With the squish of a slobbery body tackle, shoppers quickly turn from mundane consumers to parts of a larger, mycelial-like organism that can learn from the experiences of every individual member.

The infected are not undead, but they are still rabid — acrobatic, zombie-like parts of a whole that is deeply invested in expanding its membership, like Star Trek’s Borg crossed with an unhinged Cirque Du Soleil troupe. Like a colony of bees, they take instruction from Young-cheol, who tells authorities that he has infected himself with the only vaccine for the spreading virus. It’s one of Colony’s most original and intriguing ideas — a concept poised for commentary on the rise of AI, our increasingly algorithm-driven pop culture, or a more specific juxtaposition of collective vs. individualistic cultures. But the script, co-written by Yeon and Choi Gyu-seok, doesn’t deliver; rather, we’re left with an inconsistent exploration of how the hivemind processes information and emotion that muddles any potential societal insight.

The Colony script is similarly superficial and inconsistent when it comes to character exploration and dynamics, a weakness partially saved by the film’s all-star cast. Jun Ji-hyun (aka Gianna Jun of My Love From the Star fame) channels ’90s action stars as Kwon Se-jeong, a no-nonsense biotechnology professor who uses her brains and focus to try to save a ragtag group of survivors, including a trifecta of teens embroiled in a bullying plot, a retired track coach, and Se-jeong’s own ex-husband. Her most helpful allies come in the form of Ji Chang-wook’s Choi Hyun-seok, a highly competent mall security guard, and Kim Shin-rok as Choi Hyun-hee, a tech-savvy wheelchair user who is also Hyun-seok’s big sister. The brother-sister dynamic represents one of the few sustained emotional throughlines of the film.

One of Colony’s many missed opportunities when it comes to a deeper character dynamic comes in the form of Se-jeong’s relationship with her ex-husband’s current wife, Gong Seol-hee (Shin Hyun-been). Also a biotechnologist, Seol-hee is investigating the source of Young-cheol’s bioterrorist attack from the outside. The respectful dynamic subverts the usual stereotypical anonymosity seen between successive partners of the same person, but is only leaned upon occasionally, robbing their eventual team up of emotional complexity.

Where the script disappoints, Yeon’s direction delivers. Fast-paced, high-stakes action scenes maintain cohesiveness and help make the horror more anxiety-inducing. In one of the film’s early action sequences, the retired track coach character jumps, dodges, and crawls around both zombies and store endcaps in an attempt to snag some perfume that Se-jeong has identified as a possible weapon against the infected. In another, Seol-hee tries to make it out of a makeshift laboratory filled with rabid, infected monkeys in a complex, frantic scene that would slot right into a Planet of the Apes reboot film. Another one of Colony’s strengths comes in the physicality of its zombie performers, who contort their bodies into inhuman poses and collective formations. The agility of the performances, and the creativity of the choreography, imbues the infected with an alien element, increasing the creep factor as these humans act in decidedly inhuman ways.

Yeon is a director who cares about the future of cinema. He made his previous film, The Ugly, on a super-small budget , seemingly in part to experiment with ways Korean cinema might be able to survive in a time when people are going to the theaters less often and big tech streamers like Netflix have access to outsized, hard-to-compete-with budgets. For all its failures of potential, Colony is the kind of middling movie that makes for a fun low-stakes afternoon at the cinema. The premise, which is basically Die Hard with zombies, is classic; the performances are charismatic; and the direction, like the film's protagonist, gets the job done. This is no Train to Busan… but few movies are.

articles.title: After GTA 6: Extended Look Showed Rockstar's Game Running at 30fps, Tech Experts Say a 60fps Console Version Is 'Extremely Unlikely' and 'Genuinely Challenging' Even on PC
articles.summary: Getting Rockstar's hugely ambitious GTA 6 running at 60fps on current consoles will be "extremely unlikely", the tech experts at Digital Foundry have said, after analysis of footage from the Grand Theft Auto 6: Extended Look.
articles.body:
Getting Rockstar's hugely ambitious GTA 6 running at 60fps on current consoles will be "extremely unlikely", the tech experts at Digital Foundry have said, after analysis of footage from the Grand Theft Auto 6: Extended Look.

Yesterday's 27-minute reveal featured 30fps footage of the game on Netflix, YouTube, and in the raw file made available by Rockstar to download — and this is seemingly how we should all expect the game to look when it arrives on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S this November.

While 30fps might seem low compared to the frame counts of other modern gaming blockbusters, Rockstar appears to be targeting this level to maximize the sheer detail on offer in every one of those frames, Digital Foundry believes.

"It's clear that the focus was absolutely maximising the level of visual detail at a fixed 30fps frame-rate on all platforms," Digital Foundry wrote in an Extended Look deep dive article. "The rendering, simulation and presentation have all been tuned around that constraint - and the result is an unprecedented level of density, material quality and world coherence, with trade-offs landing primarily in image quality and animation smoothness rather than systemic scale or fidelity."

Specifically, the report goes on to heap praise on GTA 6's character rendering, including skin shading that makes sweat and make-up look convincing, and "huge generation improvements to hair simulation" that allows Lucia's locks to behave realistically with convincing snap-back motions, delayed follow-through and impressive "base-to-tip motion."

In terms of resolution, Digital Foundry suspects the PS5's internal rendering is clocked at 1440p without DRS, without any strong evidence of FSR 2 or TAA upscaling being used. This can lead to "a degree of softness, visible geometric aliasing and shimmer on fine details," Digital Foundry wrote, but no sign of frame-rate drops that have hampered previous entries in the series at launch. While improvements for the beefier PS5 Pro are only speculative, improved image quality and ray-tracing were mooted as more likely, over any transformative boost in performance.

"The evidence suggests that the game maintains its 33.3ms cadence with care, and Rockstar has clearly spent immense effort balancing CPU and GPU workloads to fully saturate the hardware," Digital Foundry continued. "That makes a 60fps version extremely unlikely on console hardware - there's no way to regain enough GPU and particularly CPU time to make a 16.7ms update rate work without compromising the world."

The game is carefully balanced in terms of its ambition, then, with the downside that there's likely little left in the tank to enable a 60fps mode down the line — at least on the current crop of consoles. But how about PC?

"Looking ahead to other console versions and the presumably-coming-eventually PC release, some level of caution is required," Digital Foundry wrote. "The PC platform ought to allow for higher resolutions, especially with the benefit of more modern temporal upscalers like DLSS, alongside increased RT sample counts, longer draw distances and so on. However, the CPU demands of a world this complex - tuned around console Zen 2 cores at 30fps - could make hitting 60fps genuinely challenging in a way we don't often see, and will likely require a high-end CPU like a recent Ryzen X3D to avoid bottlenecks."

articles.title: Buying a Refurbished PS5 Is Your Best Bet for a More Affordable Way to Play GTA 6 This November
articles.summary: Looking for a more affordable way to play GTA 6 this November? Here is why buying a certified refurbished PS5 is your best bet to save money on hardware right now.
articles.body:
If you're staring at the price of a new PS5 and wondering whether playing GTA 6 this November is really worth $600 or more , I'd strongly recommend looking at refurbished consoles before you do anything else.

There's simply not much value in paying full price for a brand-new PS5 right now. Sony's current pricing puts the PS5 Digital Edition at $599.99 and the disc-drive model at $649.99, while the PS5 Pro costs a frankly ridiculous $899.99.

That's a lot of money to spend if GTA 6 is the main reason you're finally jumping into the current generation. Thankfully, a reputable refurbished console can knock a meaningful chunk off that price without having to wait around for a potential price cut over Black Friday .

PlayStation 5 - Digital Edition 1TB - Certified Refurbished

My first stop right now would be PlayStation Direct , where Sony is selling certified refurbished PS5 consoles directly through its own store.

The refurbished PS5 is currently $549 , while the refurbished PS5 Digital Edition is $499 . That makes the latter particularly interesting if you're starting from scratch and don't have a collection of physical PS5 or PS4 games sitting on your shelf.

The $499 price puts it $100 below a brand-new PS5 Digital Edition, and you're getting the newer slimline design with 1TB of storage. For someone buying a console primarily to play GTA 6, that's a pretty compelling proposition.

There's nothing to fear with refurb consoles either, as, according to Sony, it'll work like new : "Every PlayStation certified refurbished product completes a rigorous recertification process that includes full testing that meets the same functional standards as new PlayStation products. Your certified refurbished product works like new."

There's another reason I'd be tempted by the Digital Edition specifically. Sony has announced plans to stop producing physical game discs for new PlayStation releases from January 2028, so we're already heading towards a future where physical games are becoming less central to the PlayStation ecosystem.

That doesn't mean physical games are suddenly going away, and I'd still recommend the disc-drive PS5 to anyone who regularly buys used games, hunts for physical discounts, borrows games from friends, or has an existing collection.

But if you're starting with a completely blank slate and GTA 6 is the game you're buying the console for, saving that additional $50 with the refurbished Digital Edition is worth considering.

PlayStation Direct isn't your only option, either. Best Buy is currently selling a refurbished PS5 for $539.99 , making it another option worth considering if you want a disc drive.

It's worth knowing exactly what you're getting here, though. This is the original 2020 PS5, with an 825GB SSD, rather than the newer slimline 1TB model sold by PlayStation Direct.

If you want the cheapest possible route into GTA 6 and don't care about physical games, I'd go for the $499 refurbished PS5 Digital Edition from PlayStation Direct . If you want a disc drive, the $539.99 Best Buy model is the cheaper option , although you're buying older hardware.

There's also a little extra incentive at Best Buy right now. The retailer is offering a $50 reward certificate when you buy GTA 6 alongside an eligible PS5 or Xbox console.

That effectively takes the sting out of the price, although I'd be careful about treating a reward certificate as the same thing as an upfront discount. You still have to spend the money initially, and the $50 comes back as Best Buy credit rather than cash.

For anyone looking to save a little extra on the PS5 Pro, there's also "Open Box" options available at Best Buy from $800.99 for a "Fair" condition, $827.99 "Good", and $854.99 "Excellent" condition . PS5 Pro consoles look pretty hard to find at most other retailers right now, so you'd be better off buying one now rather than later.

articles.title: 99 Details from The GTA 6 Extended Look
articles.summary: Love Fist, gameplay, and other Vice City memories. Here are 99 new details we spotted in the GTA 6 Extended Look:
articles.body:
We just got our clearest and most extensive look at GTA 6 yet, and there’s obviously plenty to unpack. From our first glimpses of gameplay to new characters and story insights, we’ve combed through every frame to pick out the things that matter most. There’s a lot to get through, so let’s not waste any more time. Here are 99 new details from the GTA 6 Extended Look.

1. Let’s start with the most important thing. Love Fist are back. Well, in the form of a shirt a woman is wearing towards the very end of the extended look, at least. Will we hear Jezz Torrent and the Scottish metal icons back on the radio? Who knows? But it’s good to see someone keeping the Vice City rock scene alive.

2. Moving on, yes, you can pet the dog, but you can also scold or study them, with GTA 6 bringing over Red Dead Redemption 2’s animal collection system.

3. Small actions like this all appear connected to GTA 6’s new criminal profile system, with the simple act of petting the dog accompanied by the appearance of an “angel” icon and a pleasant chime sound, an indicator Jason’s profile has been positively impacted. What we have is something that appears to be similar to Red Dead Redemption 2’s Honor system: do good (or bad) things and be shaped by those choices.

4. Bad things naturally include shooting people in the face. The new purple meter below the health bar marked with an eye icon, along with the healthy amount of slow-mo we saw in the extended look, shows us GTA 6 has been injected with its own version of Red Dead’s Dead Eye system – though GTA fans will recall Michael also had a slow-motion combat ability in GTA 5.

5. During the extended look’s final firefight, this focus ability slows down time and highlights the most efficient parts of an enemy for Jason to target; red for kill points, and yellow disarming ones.

6. There’s loads of stuff in Jason and Lucia’s fridge, and several of the items have icons that denote they can refill your characters’ gauges in some capacity, including the eye icon for the slow-mo, and a bolt, which may well relate to stamina.

7. Jason later eats from a bag of chips and regains health, like how Arthur eats in Red Dead Redemption 2 to boost his HP.

8. Talking of RDR2, it appears that particularly impressive headshots will also be highlighted in a fashion inspired by Rockstar’s western, with cinematic angles activated at specific moments.

9. During the initial drug lab bust sequence, a man is slammed through a wall, suggesting a certain level of destructibility may have been baked into some of the environments, though it’s not clear how dynamic this will be overall.

10. One of the coolest aspects of the newly-revamped gunplay is seen when Lucia reloads a shotgun one-handed while carrying a bag. Having separate reload animations for when a character is encumbered is pretty damn neat.

11. Lucia also seems deadly without a gun in either hand. We see her boxing training in action during a melee encounter, which lends her a very agile combat style.

12. Jason and Lucia can be seen robbing both a waffle house and a food mart. These are examples of smaller robberies you can do for quick cash grabs.

13. It also seems like the characters will conceal weapons behind themselves before busting a robbery, but it’s hard to say whether this is something to be activated or something that happens automatically when being observed by bystanders.

14. While robbing a jewelry store, a civilian attempts to stop Lucia by grabbing her weapon, suggesting NPCs may be less passive when witnessing your crimes and attempt to play the hero.

15. It’s taken a long time, but finally Rockstar has added a comma when writing out thousands of dollars in a GTA game. Related, there are two money indicators on the HUD - presumably, this shows how much money you are carrying on your person, and how much is in your bank account.

16. After dropping down to five in GTA 5, the wanted level is now back to being six stars in GTA 6, as was previously tradition.

17. The new wanted system also includes some additional symbols, displayed below the stars. They detail how much information the police have about you, such as if you’ve been spotted on CCTV, the clothes you are wearing, and if the police have a description of you. There are also icons that show whether you were seen as a couple, whether the police know what vehicle you’re driving, and another symbol featuring a weapon icon – presumably this means the police know to expect armed resistance.

18. The wanted stars can shift from white to red, indicating some kind of a different state of being wanted. The colour change in this extended look comes after a line of police dialogue noting they no longer have eyes on the suspect’s vehicle, suggesting it’s related to the fact you remain wanted, but aren’t actively being pursued at that moment.

19. There’s also a moment where the stars are neither whiter or red, but “hollow” – this indicates that the police do not have a description of you, but do know to respond to a crime.

20. The car icon on the wanted HUD disappears when Jason and Lucia switch from a car to a van, and the police pass close by without noticing their presence.

21. Before jumping in the van, Lucia torches the car they had been spotted in. It’s not clear whether burning the car has a gameplay utility associated with the wanted system, or is just a nice, thematic moment.

22. Putting on masks to rob a store can prevent some of the wanted symbols from appearing, and controlling the flow of incriminating data to the authorities is going to be key to managing your wanted level.

23. A revamped Item wheel allows you to select “Face Wrap” under the “Masks” category, with icons appearing elsewhere on the wheel for hats, outfits, and eyewear, and four other slots. Plus, on the bottom left, there are two icons for consumable healing items.

24. Masks aside, your escape vehicle being reported may mean you need to find a new one. Stealing cars has been totally overhauled in GTA 6, though. For instance, we know a new, tiered system applies to fancier vehicles that may need a key cloner to get into. Older cars, however, just require a slim jim to break into. Back in GTA 5, characters would occasionally use one as part of the breaking-in animation, but in GTA 6 a QTE is needed to successfully push the slim jim in and jimmy the lock. (The on-screen prompt also notes you can smash the window for a sloppier steal.)

25. Player switching appears very quick in GTA 6, as opposed to the Google Maps-esque zooming in and out from GTA 5.

26. What does resemble Google Maps, though, is the new minimap, which has a snazzy 3D view with buildings clearly visible along the streets. It may well have more polygons than the entirety of Vice City. We haven’t counted, obviously.

27. The character-switching HUD features two portraits of Jason and Lucia, side by side, with a couple of extra details: each has a horned emoji face, and a heart icon links the two portraits. The devil emojis could suggest both have a criminal profile alignment leaning “evil”, and the heart could indicate a romantic bond?

28. A button prompt to press R2 allows you to make Jason and Lucia hold hands in certain moments.

29. The extended look provided some very not-extended looks at many of the different side activities available across Leonida. Fancy some backyard wrestling, complete with John Cena’s Attitude Adjustment finisher?

31. Scuba diving returns, and you can spot an oxygen meter on the HUD. The sea is gorgeously lit and incredibly vibrant with life.

32. Lucia is shown at a gym, working out in a quick-time event, GTA: San Andreas-style.

33. We were shown some circuit racing on a bespoke track, with 16 cars on the course. The cars are in proper GT racing trim.

34. There also appears to be some kind of dedicated gun training facility.

35. A 12-vehicle off-road race is delightfully reminiscent of MotorStorm, since it’s clearly a multi-class race pitting bikes against ATVs and trucks.

36. Lucia also indulges in a spot of base jumping, providing a fantastic view of Vice City.

37. Street racing unsurprisingly returns, with a brief snippet of a six-car race showcased, featuring vehicles covered in vinyls and packing underglow. GTA 6 appears even more Midnight Club-adjacent than ever.

38. We see a party taking place for the opening of Megamundo HQ in Vice City, which appears to be a parody of real-life American Spanish-language TV network Telemundo that we can presumably tune into.

39. And if you do so, you’ll likely see some TV ads. We see a couple of examples, including a commercial for a depression drug called Angstipan. The animated brain in the antidepressant commercial looks very reminiscent of Swatpaz, an Edinburgh-based animator/comedy internet man who has cited the PS2 GTAs as an inspiration. Rockstar North people are almost certainly aware of him. A homage, or a hired fan?

40. We also see a promotion for The Prairie Sandwich from a new, Arby’s-adjacent restaurant chain called Chacey’s, expanding the fast food vendors in the GTA universe. The cowboy hat-wearing burger provides a humble 30,000 calories, and the countryside from this ad actually comes from Red Dead Redemption 2.

41. Early on, we see a man wearing gent a Righteous Slaughter: Hood Ops shirt, no doubt a follow-up to Righteous Slaughter 7, which Michael’s son plays in GTA 5. Perhaps some kind of urban, Black Ops parody? Makes more sense than Battlefield: Hard-On, I guess.

42. Multiple gang members are shown wearing S4S chains, which presumably stand for Sound4Sound, a Vice City record label. One man early on is seen wearing a blue Sound4Sound shirt.

43. There’s a fridge magnet in Jason and Lucia’s apartment for the bank company Fleeca, which you may recall robbing in the first GTA Online heist.

44. The bikini-clad woman from the cover art of the original GTA: Vice City can be seen reversed in a picture frame in Lucia’s apartment beside the TV.

45. We see quite a few people wearing turquoise Manatees sportswear, which is Vice City’s version of the Miami Dolphins.

46. Identified weapons include the Moreland 850 shotgun and Duke 556 assault rifle. The Duke Arms Company is a firearms manufacturer from Red Dead Online, and it appears GTA is leaning towards more fictional branding for its weapons, as it does for its cars.

47. There’s a very short glimpse of a console dashboard, and we can see a prominent logo for Space Monkey 3: Bananas Gone Bad, which is a game that was introduced in GTA Online.

48. Let’s now dig into the story and its key players, and where better to start than with GTA 6’s two protagonists, Jason and Lucia. We know their love story will play a huge role in GTA 6, but keeping this relationship strong may not be so simple.

49. Jason and Lucia are picking up drugs for Boobie Ike, suggesting he’ll be one of GTA 6’s quest givers.

50. At a rooftop bar, the couple meets Brian and Lori Heder, who are married and have known Jason for a long time. Brian is a drug smuggler, and it's fair to assume we’ll be doing some jobs for him, too.

51. Halfway through, Jason and Lucia can be seen picking up Raul Bautista, a mastermind bank robber that we’ll no doubt be executing jobs with. We can see him in a shootout alongside Jason a little later on, suggesting things may not always go to plan.

52. We also get a look at another mission where it appears we’ll be hired as bodyguards for Andrés de León, who appears to be some kind of media bigshot important enough to be targeted by armed assailants at a Megamundo party.

53. This modern-day version of Vice City isn’t just about meeting new faces, but visiting new places too – along with some spots that will likely be familiar to GTA fans. We see Jason and Lucia chilling on what could potentially be Vice Point, Ocean Beach, or Washington Beach. At another point, we see Jason dive off a jetty with dolphins frolicking in the distance. There seems to be a literal ocean of opportunities for fun outside of the main story.

54. The exclusive rooftop bar featured heavily in the extended look is named “Effluvia”. As it turns out, the definition of Effluvia is “an unpleasant smell.” The clientele might stink, but the view certainly doesn’t.

55. 12 minutes in, we get a good look at Starfish Island. You probably remember this prominent piece of real estate from GTA: Vice City, since it was home to its Hawaiian-shirt-loving drug baron, Ricardo Diaz. Might Jason and Lucia have their own hideaway there amidst the sprawling mansions and private tennis courts?

56. Continuing the GTA series’ proud tradition of featuring shops and restaurants with delightfully pun-based names, we can spot Lickety Split ice cream parlour. Banana splits served quick? Or something far more sexual? You decide!

57. One neon sign out the front of a club says “Cortez”. This could potentially be a nod to Juan Cortez, the retired colonel from GTA: Vice City. However, it’s also possible that it’s a bar owned by his daughter and notorious party girl, Mercedes. That’s assuming she actually survived the ’80s.

58. There’s a huge cruise ship out on the water around halfway through. We’re used to GTA loving a cargo ship infiltration mission, but are they mixing it up here? Can we board it?

59. Back to that view from Effluvia, though. Just look at it! GTA 6 seems to have more picturesque views than a postcard stand. Not only does the draw distance seem near-infinite, but there’s just so much life on display – particularly in the various aircraft in the skies above.

60. It wouldn’t be GTA without some puerile humour. As longtime lovers of the high art of low-brow, here are all the sordid references we’ve spotted so far, starting with Palm & Flute, parodying the Arm & Hammer brand of cleaning products, and obviously a reference to self-care.

61. On the same early drug den table, we can see that familiar pest control company Bugstars has its own line of products, including RATOUT rat poison. As in, “get your.” As in, give your rodent an airing .

62. A classic returns: Gruppe 6, or Gruppe Sechs, as it was styled in the 3D universe, is a secure transit firm with a name that sounds remarkably like the other sort of gang banging.

63. Why sixty-nine when you can Nine 1 Nine? We see an airbound advertisment for a Vice City night club spot, which takes a rather forward position on positions .

64. A Vice City strip club is called Jack of Hearts. As in, jack-off arts. As in, the noble art of the hand dance.

65. There’s a DVD beneath Lucia’s TV for a movie called Edged, which is arguably how we’ve been feeling since Rockstar first revealed this game back in 2023.

66. There’s also a book on her coffee table called Two Pricks in the Bush. We don’t have to explain this one, right?

67. And finally, there’s one lad grinding one out to VR smut.

68. We immediately see an NPC sitting on the rear of a car in the first few seconds; can we expect a greater variety of ways we’ll spot people interacting with stationary cars around the world?

69. Window decals have been glimpsed in previous trailers but are immediately visible again here; hopefully we have good control over their placement.

70. Many of the cars throughout this extended look are familiar, like the Bobcat and Rumpo you can spot straight away in this scene, but plenty are fresh – such as a Willard model that was first seen in GTA: San Andreas and later in GTA 4. Willard was re-introduced into GTA Online with models that riffed on Buick, but this Willard is new.

71. We spotted several Leonida city tour buses throughout, including one on the left at around nine minutes in. We can’t wait to commandeer one, but can we ride on them, too?

72. About a third of the way through the footage, there’s a car being towed on the right as a street fight causes traffic chaos. A tow truck appears again later, dragging what looks like the same coloured car.

73. We later spot another tow truck attending what appears to be a possible breakdown on a bridge. Combined with GTA 6’s dense traffic and more realistically scaled roads, the atmosphere of GTA 6’s driving component definitely seems more credible and authentic.

74. The quality of car cabins is incredible, with no interior detail seemingly spared, from rear passenger window controls to working pedals.

75. The impressive details continue on the outside, too, and we can see working turn signals on the cars.

76. This is just as well, since there are highway warning signs reminding all drivers that “Turn signals are now required in Leonida.”

77. Speaking of turning, check out what happens with Lucia’s hair as the mild cornering force causes it to sway to the right.

78. By the way, the license plate on Jason’s Sentinel says “Discover Gloriana”, indicating the car comes from interstate. Does Gloriana neighbour Leonida, and might we see any of it?

79. Car chases seem to be even more crazy and exciting, with shooting out tyres shown to induce multiple rollovers in quick succession. Not only does it look super effective; it looks amazing in action.

80. Can we use the mobility scooters that we can see some of Vice City’s population driving? Rockstar has to know everyone will want to at one point.

81. We can see some electric scooters from a cinematic angle. Surely we’ll be able to ride these.

82. Air boats will no doubt be the perfect way to move through the shallow swamps, as seen two-thirds of the way through the extended look.

83. We see Lucia on a jet ski, the perfect way to show the world you hate the ocean.

84. Kayaking seems like a nice way to slow things down a bit, and moving through a heavily trafficked waterway in such a small craft certainly gives the world a fabulous sense of scale

85. Late in the trailer, we see the Lure Predator boat, which looks like the perfect fishing vessel.

GTA 6 Reveal: 15 New Screenshots, Including 1 Exclusive on IGN

86. We don’t know exactly how many songs GTA 6 is set to feature, but it’s going to be an undoubtedly mammoth soundtrack, and the extended look featured a salvo of songs we now know are in the game, including Pop Bottles by Birdman and Lil Wayne, and the following tracks:

87. Let Your Love Flow by The Bellamy Brothers

90. Pound Town, by Sexyy Red and Tay Keith

93. But I Think It's a Dream by Captain & Tennille

96. Off the Grid, by !!! (Chk Chk Chk) and Meah Pace

98. Inner Light, by Elderbrook and Bob Moses

99. And, finally, as is GTA tradition, the music of Phil Collins can be heard in an elevator with the classic Against All Odds. His songs can be heard in GTA: Vice City Stories, GTA 4, and GTA 5. Collins famously played himself in Vice City Stories, which culminated in a mission featuring a live performance of In the Air Tonight. He was the first celebrity to play themselves in a Grand Theft Auto game.

And that was everything we managed to find after taking a magnifying glass to this extended look trailer for Grand Theft Auto VI. What are some of your favourite details? Did you spot anything we missed? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: 6 More Magic: The Gathering Crossovers We Want in Universes Beyond
articles.summary: With MTG’s Universes Beyond lineup expanding, here are 7 more ideal fantasy and sci-fi crossovers we want to see, including Narnia, The Cosmere, and The Elder Scrolls.
articles.body:
Not too long ago, we put together a wishlist of seven Magic: The Gathering crossovers we'd love to see in Universes Beyond ( whether that's in 2027 or in the next few years). Well, I've been thinking about it again, and, frankly, there are still far too many great possibilities out there to stop at seven.

With Magic's Universes Beyond lineup continuing to expand, I've decided to throw six more potential crossovers into the ring. Some are obvious, some are perhaps a little more out there, but all of them feel like they'd fit surprisingly well into Magic's increasingly expansive multiverse.

As we covered in that original wishlist, we know Magic has three more Universes Beyond sets lined up for 2027, arriving in April, August, and November.

Hasbro CEO Chris Cocks has also suggested that next year's crossovers will be "a bit more fantasy-adjacent", following feedback from fans on some of the more recent collaborations.

That still leaves a huge amount of room for speculation, and more than enough fantasy worlds we'd love to see collide with Magic. So, here's our sequel: six more Universes Beyond crossovers we'd love to see.

Starting things off, The Elder Scrolls. While we are still painstakingly awaiting The Elder Scrolls VI , an eventual crossover with Magic: The Gathering wouldn't be beyond the realms of imagination, especially if we're talking epic fantasy.

Bethesda has already partnered with Magic as part of the Universes Beyond: Fallout set, so extending that partnership to Bethesda's other gaming titan... It just works.

Honestly, I probably should have included this in the original article. I can absolutely see this happening in the near future. Whether that's in 2027, or whenever The Elder Scrolls VI eventually releases in the (fingers crossed) next few years.

Okay, admittedly, this is one of my more "out there" picks for a Magic: The Gathering crossover. It's absolutely fantasy-adjacent, but its 21st-century setting may put off more than a few diehard Magic fans. Still, I'm going to die on this hill, because I genuinely think Supernatural could make for a fantastic Universes Beyond set.

The show's mythology almost already feels tailor-made. Magic has Angels and Demons as established creature types, while the show's spells, rituals, curses and supernatural artefacts could slot neatly into the game's existing card types. Then you've got 15 seasons of monsters, supernatural creatures and a ridiclously extensive cast of characters to draw from. It pretty much sorts itself at this rate.

Plus, Universes Beyond has already shown that Magic can accommodate worlds that look and feel very different from its traditional fantasy settings. If anything, the show's grimy Americana, roadside diners, abandoned churches, forests and endless motel rooms could give the set a visual identity unlike anything else in Magic.

Beyond all that, Supernatural was an absolutely massive part of the TV landscape for years, and the nostalgia for it is very real. A set like this would be tapping into a fanbase that grew up with Sam and Dean, making it a potentially huge nostalgia play for both Supernatural fans and new Magic players.

If Wizards of the Coast really is looking to lean further into fantasy with its next Universes Beyond sets, then The Chronicles of Narnia feels like an obvious contender. It's difficult to think of many properties that fit Magic's traditional fantasy aesthetic quite as naturally, with talking animals, witches, kings, mythical creatures and epic battles all baked into the world of Narnia.

There's also a huge amount of material to work with across the seven books, from Aslan, the Pevensie siblings and the White Witch to Mr. Tumnus, Caspian, Reepicheep and the countless creatures of Narnia. And while the books are decades old , the movies from the 2000s mean there's a hefty dose of nostalgia here too. Plus, there's that Greta Gerwig adaptation upcoming in 2027 as well.

Narnia feels like exactly the kind of crossover that could appeal to both longtime Magic players and a whole new audience, while being one of the easiest Universes Beyond properties to slot into Magic's fantasy world.

If we're talking about properties that could tap into a serious well of nostalgia, Buffy the Vampire Slayer feels like another strong contender. Like Supernatural, it's a modern setting that might seem a little strange alongside Magic's traditional fantasy worlds, but the actual subject matter fits surprisingly well... again!

Vampires, demons, witches, werewolves, ghosts and a whole host of other supernatural nasties would give Wizards plenty to work with. Albeit, again, similarly to Supernatural, so I wouldn't expect to see both in Universes Beyond.

Brandon Sanderson’s Cosmere Universe feel tailor-made for Universes Beyond. Sanderson has previously said that WotC reached out for a potential partnership, but progress stalled a couple of years ago due to other projects taking priority.

Whether split into distinct Mistborn and Stormlight Archive Commander decks within a complete set, or launched as a full tentpole release for each series, this feels like a match made in heaven.

Because Sanderson is an outspoken MTG player , who has previously written official lore for Wizards of the Coast , the connection goes far deeper than basic brand synergy as well.

So, this seems like another sure bet to me, if both parties can get things up and running again.

If Wizards really does want to lean into more fantasy-adjacent Universes Beyond sets, Robert Jordan's sprawling fantasy world seems almost tailor-made for Magic. Somehow I'm also mentioning Brandon Sanderson again as well, who famously stepped in to bring Jordan's masterwork across the finish line .

The Wheel of Time gives you an enormous amount of material to work with, so this seems like an easy fit, whether that's in 2027, or beyond that. And with the recent Amazon series introducing the world to a new generation of fans, the timing feels pretty good too. If only they hadn't cancelled it, it was getting really good!

Those are our new predictions/ additions to the wistlist, but what are you expecting from Universes Beyond in the coming years? Let us know in the comments!

articles.title: Nvidia's DLSS 5 Leaks Online, and Modders Have Already Turned It Into a Slop Filter
articles.body:
Nvidia debuted DLSS 5 back in March 2026 , promising to bring neural rendering to games in order to make them look more realistic. While pretty much everyone hated it, it seems like Nvidia has continued to work on it behind the scenes: It's leaked in a build of the NBA 2K27 beta.

Twitter user @renan_maniero spotted the new DLSS file in the NBA 2K27 early access, called nvngx_dlssnr.dll. The 'nr' at the end there appears to stand for neural rendering. Just finding the file in the game's directory would be one thing, but it looks like some enterprising modders have been able to build it into some other existing games.

Eita, o acesso antecipado do jogo NBA 2K27 veio com uma DLL nova do DLSS. DLSS-NR (Neural Rendering) 👀 pic.twitter.com/X15fYO92RU — Renan Maniero (@renan_maniero) August 26, 2026

Eita, o acesso antecipado do jogo NBA 2K27 veio com uma DLL nova do DLSS. DLSS-NR (Neural Rendering) 👀 pic.twitter.com/X15fYO92RU

Some modders built a DLSS 5 mod and integrated it into Control , which was spotted by Gizmodo . In the initial post on X, you can see the modders manipulating some sliders to change the degree by which the neural renderer is changing the image. Things like auto skin mask, intensity and style are all customizable, which is something Nvidia said would be possible when it announced the technology earlier this year.

A YouTube video shows the mod in action, and from the moment neural rendering is enabled, the frame rate is cut nearly in half – from 95fps to 53. Keep in mind that right now the mod is limited to character models, and it really only has the effect of making Jessie look like she needs a nap.

Over on the Nvidia subreddit , some modders were able to work the tech into The Last of Us Part 2, and while most of the images with the tech enabled make the characters look downright weird, the response seems to be split down the middle. One user says the DLSS 5 "looks deep fried, I am not going to lie," which is probably where I'm sitting. Someone else says, "There's more detail and the characters look more photo realistic and less like Pixar characters."

Obviously, this technology is in its very early stages, and once game developers are able to actually work it into the game naturally and optimize it, there probably won't be such a pronounced performance impact. But it's hard to imagine that turning on DLSS 5 will in any way improve your frame rate, which makes it one of the first pieces of Nvidia's AI software suite that makes performance worse .

Either way, now that the DLL file that enables the technology is clearly out in the wild, it's only a matter of time before it actually makes its way to market. But if the RTX 5090 gets its performance cut in half, I don't know if I'd recommend anyone enable it until some future graphics card hits the market.

Because while the visual effect the tech has will probably be debated until the end of time, the performance impact is where PC gamers tend to decide whether or not tech is worth using. It took a few years for people to start actually turning ray tracing on, as it was a surefire way to halve your performance in its early days. I'll be testing the technology one way or another as soon as Nvidia actually releases it.

Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

articles.body:
If you're already planning to spend $100 on the GTA 6 Ultimate Edition, I've spotted a pretty painless way to knock $5 off the price before you've even placed your preorder.

Amazon is currently selling a $100 PlayStation Store gift card for $95 for Prime members , giving you an instant $5 saving that you can put towards your GTA 6 preorder. It's not going to change your life, but if you're going to spend the money anyway, you may as well get $5 of it back.

$100 PlayStation Store Gift Card [Digital Code]

The maths is particularly simple if you're planning to buy the $99.99 GTA 6 Ultimate Edition . Buy the gift card for $95, use that $100 of PlayStation Store credit to pay for the game, and you've effectively saved five bucks.

It's worth noting that this particular offer is for Prime members , so make sure you're signed into the right Amazon account before checking out. And, as ever with these gift card discounts, I'd recommend checking the final price at checkout before placing your order in case the promotion has changed.

All GTA 6 preorders come with the Vintage Vice City Pack, which includes a classic car, outfits and hairstyles for Jason and Lucia, and an exclusive weapon pattern.

'55 Vapid Stanier: A classic sedan that can be stored at the Shore Court garage.

Outfits and hairstyles: Jason gets a vintage pastel linen suit, while Lucia gets a red sequin mini dress and matching hairstyle.

Exclusive weapon pattern: A tropical design inspired by Tommy Vercetti's famous palm-tree shirt.

Note that the Vintage Vice City Pack is included with all digital purchases of GTA 6 made before November 20, 2026, so you don't necessarily need to preorder today to get it.

articles.summary: The Xbox Series X25 anniversary console is officially up for pre-order, so you know what that means: scalpers are cashing in.
articles.body:
The Xbox Series X25 anniversary console is officially up for pre-order, so you know what that means: scalpers are cashing in.

Like clockwork, pre-order pages for Microsoft's 25th anniversary console were bombarded by buyers when they went live yesterday, August 27, 2026. At $899.99 for that translucent green box and $79.99 for its themed controller, the price to celebrate Xbox's birthday was already quite steep, but scalpers have still seemingly managed to find buyers willing to spend thousands.

In the 24 hours since pre-order pages went live, multiple listings have popped up on eBay and, in many cases, successfully sold the Xbox Series X25 console bundle for more than $2,000. One scalper selling the full package – which Microsoft said comes with the "XBOX 25" branded 1TB console and controller, as well as a copy of Halo: Campaign Evolved – managed to successfully close a listing for $2,800. Many, many others have managed to sell their confirmed purchases for around $2,500.

That's a remarkable increase for an already pricey Xbox console, but the individual controller is getting hit just as hard. If you want to pick up one of the controllers (which also happen to have the original Xbox logo hidden in the back) from eBay, you could be spending as much as $185, more than double its retail cost. Many others are going for around $130.

"This collection is our way of celebrating the community that has made XBOX what it is today," Microsoft said when detailing its X25 collection earlier this week. "Thank you for being part of this journey."

Unfortunately, direct pre-orders for the release from retailers like Amazon and Best Buy seem to be largely sold out, at least for now. It's also not a surprise to see scalpers hitting the X25 collection as hard as they are. Valve's new Steam controller and Steam Machine were hit particularly hard when they launched earlier this year. Even the upcoming Grand Theft Auto 6 was hit by scalpers despite Rockstar Games confirming it will only release GTA 6 digitally.

The difference between the X25 release and things like Pokémon cards or the Steam Machine is there's no guarantee that Microsoft has any plans to produce more Xbox anniversary consoles. This seems like an extremely limited release, giving scalpers the perfect opportunity to strike while the iron's hot and make a quick buck. The company has also confirmed each console features its own unique engraving.

The Xbox 25th anniversary collection launches November 13, 2026, with its standalone controller set to arrive earlier come October 20. Target reportedly had some employees slicing open Pokémon card boxes to discourage scalping behavior earlier this month. One Disney store in London had to temporarily close after a few scalpers got "aggressive" toward others .

Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

articles.title: Everything Coming to Peacock in September
articles.body:
Peacock recently raised all of its subscription pricing , so you may be looking to September's slate of releases to see just what that price increase gets you. The short answer is that you'll be getting much of the same from Peacock next month. YouTube Premium isn't getting added to the service until early 2027, and the highly anticipated Dungeon Crawler Carl series is even further away.

What you will get is Universal Pictures movies , NBC shows, and a couple of Peacock Originals. If you're wondering what's worth watching, we've gathered together some of our top picks right here. You can also jump to all of the new releases for September for the full list by day.

Happy Death day is a time travel horror movie that is quite entertaining. If you're looking for something fun to kick off the spooky season early, it's worth a watch. Here's what we said in our review :

"Happy Death Day is a deliciously wicked treat with fun twists and a strong lead performance by Jessica Rothe. It won’t scare you, but it will entertain you with a cynical sense of humor and a few clever new twists on a familiar formula." - William Bibbiani

What more can really be said about the Twilight movies ? The first adaptation of Stephenie Meyer's popular YA book series is just as bad as you remember, but it's what put Robert Pattinson on the map. The following four movies did get better, and it's just one of those franchises that you have to go back and rewatch sometimes. There may be better vampire movies out there , but there's only one Twilight.

The Paper: Season 2 Premiere - September 9

The Paper is a mockumentary-style TV series set in the same universe as The Office. This is the only big Peacock Original for September. The premiere of season 2 comes after a well-received season 1, which we loved in our 8 out of 10 review last year :

"The first season of The Paper (the first of several, I hope) is getting an 8. Ironically, a show about the place of ink-and-paper journalism in a social media era is weaker because it’s clearly wanting to be a 20+ episode season kind of show that fell victim to dropping in the binge-and-stream era. The tried and true formula creator Greg Daniels has honed across a handful of successful series is on full display in The Paper. The character archetypes you’d expect from an Office spin-off are here, as is the easy sense of positivity and that change for the good is possible that you might expect from the creator of Parks and Rec. Maybe it moves a little too briskly for its own good, arriving at places we can all see coming, but they’re satisfying places and it’s funny the whole trip." - Clint Gage

You're either a fan of Wes Anderson movies or you're not, there's not really any inbetween. For those who love what the director has to offer, his latest film The Phoenician scheme is arriving later this month. Here's what we said in our review:

"A new Wes Anderson movie is always an event, but the writer-director’s latest whirligig comedy, The Phoenician Scheme, might be his slightest in a couple decades. Benicio del Toro is predictably deadpan (maybe too deadpan) as a powerful 1950s European robber baron beset by assassins and intent on passing down his entire empire and inheritance to his estranged daughter. Much of the rest of the extended Anderson acting troupe shows up in minor roles, as usual, while Michael Cera makes a particularly amusing debut in Wes World as a Norwegian bug expert along for the wild ride. As with all of Anderson’s comedies, this one has big laughs, visual invention, and some startlingly dark moments. But it also can’t help but look like a minor disappointment after the richer Asteroid City. The major problem: There’s just not much to del Toro’s character, a Royal Tenenbaum without the spunk." - A.A. Dowd

articles.title: Capcom Is Making Life-Sized Statues of Lady Dimitrescu and Albert Wesker, and the Internet Is Being Totally Normal About It
articles.summary: Capcom is making thirsty fans’ dreams come true for Resident Evil’s 30th anniversary exhibition, revealing that it will display life-sized statues of Lady Dimitrescu and Albert Wesker.
articles.body:
Capcom is making thirsty fans’ dreams come true for Resident Evil’s 30th anniversary exhibition, revealing that it will display life-sized statues of Lady Dimitrescu and Albert Wesker.

There’s something for everyone at Capcom’s RE anniversary extravaganza. Coming to the Shibuya BEAM Gallery from October 30 to December 24, the exhibition will feature real-life recreations of iconic items and creatures from the famous horror game franchise, including “life-sized models of villains crafted with meticulous detail,” as told by SaigaNAK .

Two of these villains have been revealed, and the reactions from the internet have not disappointed.

As posted on the exhibition's official website in late August, Resident Evil antagonist Albert Wesker and Village’s Lady Dimitrescu are getting life-sized statues at the Shibuya exhibition. Concept art for these sculptures have also been shared, showing Lady D sitting in an ornate, plush chair while Wesker stands tall, wearing his iconic sunglasses and trenchcoat combo.

It appears that both villains will be located in the Evidence of Horror section of the exhibition; Wesker is reportedly placed in the “parasites and biological threats” zone, while Lady Dimitrescu sits in the “zone dedicated to fungi and hallucinations.”

What’s more, Lady D’s statue is reportedly 290 centimeters tall (approximately nine and a half feet) — though it’s unclear if that will be the true height of the sculpture, given that she’s in a seated position.

Naturally, the internet wasted no time telling the whole world all about their upcoming heists of these statues.

“They better put it in bulletproof glass,” one user joked of Dimitrescu’s statue on X. Another simply posted a GIF from National Treasure, showing Nick Cage saying his iconic line: “I’m gonna steal the Declaration of Independence.”

“If true, they are gonna need 'round the clock security for that thing, because I KNOW multiple people will try to run a heist for it,” another remarked .

me to the life sized alcina dimitrescu statue at the world of biohazard 30th anniversary exhibition pic.twitter.com/hMW249Zrtb

So a lifesize mother Dimitrescu statue will be at the Biohazard expedition in Japan. pic.twitter.com/aJIBXoPryq — CJKnight Requiem Collector (@slc_knight) August 28, 2026

So a lifesize mother Dimitrescu statue will be at the Biohazard expedition in Japan. pic.twitter.com/aJIBXoPryq

Somehow, these replies aren’t as freaky as the comments regarding Leon Kennedy’s life-sized statue, which will also be displayed at the Shibuya exhibition. (You can imagine how that went down when it got announced earlier this month. We fear Capcom will legitimately need 24/7 security for that particular sculpture.)

In the meantime, fans can get their Resident Evil fix by checking out our interview with Zach Cregger about his upcoming movie adaptation of the franchise, which comes to theaters next month .

articles.title: Chun-Li Actress Grew Her Thighs 6.5 Centimeters to Match the First Lady of Fighting Games for the Street Fighter Movie
articles.summary: Callina Liang, who plays Chun-Li in Legendary’s upcoming Street Fighter movie, revealed the protein-heavy diet and intense workout routine she followed to bring the First Lady of Fighting Games to life.
articles.body:
Callina Liang, who plays Chun-Li in Legendary’s upcoming Street Fighter movie , revealed the protein-heavy diet and intense workout routine she followed to bring the First Lady of Fighting Games to life.

If there’s one thing Chun-Li is known for — besides being the Strongest Woman in the World, of course — it’s her thick, muscular thunder thighs, which have only gotten more impressive with each new Street Fighter game. From Third Strike to Street Fighter V and now Street Fighter 6 , it’s clear the devs at Capcom have a clear vision in mind for the character’s physical appearance. (And we thank them for it.)

Callina Liang knew this was an important thing to get right, so she buckled down and began following a strict martial arts workout routine and eating a high-protein diet to help grow her muscles — to the point where she almost got sick.

Street Fighter: Cast Revealed for Legendary's Live-Action Movie

"Chun-Li is all kicks. So we did a bunch of Taekwondo training, Muay Thai, and Wushu (Kung Fu). I did two hours of that a day and strengthened my legs a lot and changed my diet drastically. When I was bulking, I ate 12 eggs a day. Every two hours I had to have a meal, and I was on the verge of throwing up. But it worked. By the end of the shoot, my thighs had grown six-and-a-half centimeters each,” she said in an August interview with Empire Magazine.

That’s not all; Liang did her homework and downloaded every single Street Fighter game onto her PlayStation 5, where she recorded all of the character’s moves to make her fight scenes as accurate as possible.

"I downloaded every single version of Street Fighter onto a PS5 and I recorded all of Chun-Li's moves during fights on my phone in slow-mo, so I could play them back and study them," she added.

Liang isn’t the only actor who put in major time to make their Street Fighter performance perfect; David Dastmalchian, who plays the series’ recurring villain, M. Bison, told us that he did deep research to deliver a version of the psycho-powered dictator that leans heavily into a cult-leader archetype.

“I don’t want to be just another one of these bad guys, cut from the typical cloth,” he said. “How do you have all of these people willing to go into battle for you, die for you? …we dug in and studied really insane dictators over time, thinking about everyone from idamine all the way back to fascist Italy in World War II, and looking at not just movie characters but real, historical characters,” he said during a chat with IGN’s Tom Jorgensen at San Diego Comic Con .

Legendary’s Street Fighter flick releases in theaters on October 16, 2026. It’ll be the second Capcom property getting a theatrical release this year, with Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil beginning screenings on September 18.

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 Is Already Bringing Back Characters from GTA 5
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 will feature at least one character from GTA Online.
articles.body:
Grand Theft Auto 6 will feature at least one character from GTA Online.

In Rockstar's extended look at GTA 6, fans were introduced to a bunch of characters with a wide range of morals. One character that fans probably overlooked is Valentina, a woman who was introduced last year in GTA Online. She makes her debut in a cutscene for the Money Fronts update, where she can be seen hopping off a private jet and interacting with Mr. Faber. While her role didn't seem especially significant at the time, it looks like she'll have a larger part to play in GTA 6.

The character hires Jason and Lucia to be security for a VIP who is attending a party that is inevitably disrupted by gun-wielding goons. It's unclear if Valentina will have a larger role in GTA 6 outside of this mission, but it wouldn't be surprising if she did. It also raises the question of what else, or who else, Rockstar has been planting in GTA Online all these years. Of course, fans are hopeful to see Michael, Franklin, and Trevor return in GTA 6, but it remains to be seen if that will actually happen.

Valentina is the first GTA Online character confirmed to return in GTA 6. #GTAVI pic.twitter.com/CbzzQAudDF — GTA Wiki (@GTAWikiOfficial) August 27, 2026

Valentina is the first GTA Online character confirmed to return in GTA 6. #GTAVI pic.twitter.com/CbzzQAudDF

GTA 5 and GTA Online featured a handful of characters from GTA 4, including Brucie, Karen, Packie, and more. It wouldn't be surprising if Rockstar continues this same strategy and we see small side characters from the previous games in GTA 6. We likely won't get definitive answers on this until release, but this small reveal will certainly lead to rampant speculation.

In related news, IGN has heaps of other GTA 6-related news following the extended look. We got an exclusive preview of the game , an interview with Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson , and a variety of breakdowns on the game's various systems and details. Rockstar also confirmed that GTA 6 playthroughs can last as long as 80 hours , if not even longer, so you can expect to spend an outrageous amount of time in Leonida when the game releases in November.

articles.title: Pokemon Tales: The Misadventures of Sirfetch’d and Pichu Will Be Exclusive to Disney+
articles.summary: The upcoming stop-motion series will stream exclusively on Disney+ and DisneyXD, as revealed in a special showcase during PokémonXP.
articles.body:
The upcoming stop-motion series will stream exclusively on Disney+ and DisneyXD, as revealed in a special showcase during PokémonXP.

PokémonXP is underway, marking the debut of the very first fan convention completely dedicated to all things Pokémon. Of course, some exclusive reveals and big announcements are expected, and one of those involves the brand’s next big animated series.

First announced in July 2025, The Misadventures of Sirfetch’d and Pichu is exactly what it sounds like — a charming, humorous romp that follows the two Pokémon as they get into all sorts of hijinks in Galar.

As revealed at PokémonXP, the series will be streamed exclusively on Disney+ and the DisneyXD channel. This was an unexpected turn of events, as the brand’s first stop motion series, Pokémon Concierge, is streamed solely on Netflix.

This new show is being made in collaboration between The Pokémon Company International and Aardman Animations, a British stop-motion animation studio best known for beloved properties like Wallace and Gromit and Shaun the Sheep.

As told during the show’s behind-the-scenes panel at PokémonXD, there are 262 people working on the project at any given time. Each animator achieves roughly 13.5 of animation per week, with each episode taking 110 weeks to complete. Three episodes are usually in production simultaneously, allowing the crew to get as much work done as possible.

Pokémon Tales: The Misadventures of Sirfetch’d & Pichu, our new stop-motion animated series with @aardman , is coming to @DisneyPlusUK in 2027! 🛡️⚡ Join our unlikely heroes, Sirfetch’d and Pichu, in their gallant quest to protect Pokémon across Galar. pic.twitter.com/D3UBkZ3pBE — Pokémon UK (@PokemonNewsUK) August 28, 2026

Pokémon Tales: The Misadventures of Sirfetch’d & Pichu, our new stop-motion animated series with @aardman , is coming to @DisneyPlusUK in 2027! 🛡️⚡ Join our unlikely heroes, Sirfetch’d and Pichu, in their gallant quest to protect Pokémon across Galar. pic.twitter.com/D3UBkZ3pBE

The panel also showed off the very first animation tests for both Pichu and SirFetch’d, as well as an official trailer for the show, which will release sometime in 2027.

The series' official logline reads: "Our heroes embark on a gallant quest to help and protect Pokémon across the region. Their missions rarely go as planned, but their noble deeds forge their friendship as they step bravely into the unknown. Peril, alliances, rivalries, extraordinary Pokémon, and endless laughs await them."

As told by the folks at Aardman, Escavalier will serve as the main antagonist of the series, which they described as a “knight that could challenge and compete against” Sirfetch’d.

“What I love is the personalities we’re giving to all these characters," James Young of Aardman Animations said. "I'm really excited for the Pokémon family, and for all of you and to see how you like them, to see the personalities we’ve given to these Pokémon characters in our world."

Pokemon Concierge was also confirmed for a second season back in 2025, set to air on Netflix this September.

articles.title: Rockstar Approached Netflix for Exclusive GTA 6 Extended Look, Not the Other Way Around
articles.summary: The big Grand Theft Auto 6 extended look (mostly) went off without a hitch, and apparently, it was Rockstar Games' idea to bring it to Netflix in the first place, not the other way around.
articles.body:
The big Grand Theft Auto 6 extended look ( mostly ) went off without a hitch, and apparently, it was Rockstar Games' idea to bring it to Netflix in the first place, not the other way around.

Amidst the unprecedented amount of hype for GTA 6, there was a fair amount of confusion from fans, who questioned Rockstar's decision to make its gameplay debut a Netflix exclusive for six hours after its premiere yesterday. This first real look at Jason and Lucia's story definitely managed to wow viewers, but even after 27 minutes of Vice City, the question remained: Why Netflix?

Many assumed it to be a high-value deal cooked up by the streaming giant to pull eyes its way, but apparently, that's not the case. A Rockstar PR representative told Kinda Funny Games ahead of the big reveal that it was actually the GTA 6 developer's idea to stream the extended look on Netflix. The quote is: "We wanted to go to Netflix."

It's a response that may generate more questions than answers. Rockstar first raised eyebrows when it confirmed plans to bring GTA 6: Extended Look exclusively to Netflix earlier this month, promising what eventually turned out to be a lengthy version of a long-awaited third trailer – but only for subscribers. Even with the knowledge that the full presentation would eventually drop on YouTube just a few hours later, fans who have been waiting 13 years for the next Grand Theft Auto were annoyed to hear they'd have to wait even longer if they didn't want to fork over the cash.

"This is unbelievably scummy," said one fan on X at the time. "Everyone is excited for the extended look of GTA 6, but it's premiering on Netflix first, which will influence people to get a subscription. This needs to be called out, because if any other studio, such as Bethesda, did this, they would be crucified."

Still, some were willing to be patient and see if there might be something more to Rockstar's grand plan. At least some of the hesitation then turned to excitement after Strauss Zelnick, CEO of parent company Take-Two Interactive, promised that the extended look would be worth the price for early admission .

He went as far as to say that the plan was "an example of Rockstar trying new things" as marketing for GTA 6 truly kicked off. He also told Bloomberg , "I think when the title is launched on Netflix, if you watch it, you'll understand more."

"If you're not a Netflix subscriber, you definitely should be one," he told IGN at the time. "And as for the trailer itself, it's coming soon enough that I'll let you arrive at your own conclusion."

Well, the trailer is here, and while it certainly managed to impress, it's still not clear why Rockstar felt the need to bring GTA 6: Extended Look to Netflix, specifically. That said, there are still months to go before launch arrives. Nothing about the developer's future marketing plans has been revealed yet, so it's possible we could see other entries or even episodes added to Extended Look in the future.

For now, though, all we know is that Rockstar has its reasons. IGN got an early peak at all things GTA 6 ahead of yesterday's gameplay reveal and walked away just about as impressed as everyone else. You can check out our thoughts in our preview , and then be sure to see what we had to ask the developer in our interview . You can also check out 69 details we learned while visiting Rockstar HQ , the GTA Online character who's making a comeback , and the Red Dead Redemption 2 Easter Egg hidden in the extended look .
